+  We first establish the asymptotic needed for
+  \textup{(ii)}\(\Rightarrow\)\textup{(iii)}. This conclusion is also
+  obtainable from Charlier--Kreczman's quotient-limit mechanism
+  \cite[Proposition~10 and Remark~12]{CharlierKreczman2025}; we give the
+  coefficient-level argument because the residue thresholds and positivity
+  are part of the hypotheses used here.
+
+  \emph{Peripheral period.}
+  The classical power characterization of weak Perron numbers gives an
+  integer \(h\ge1\) for which
+  \[
+    \rho:=\beta^h
+  \]
+  is a Perron number \cite{Brunotte2013,Lind1984}. Equivalently, if
+  \(\gamma\) is any conjugate of \(\beta\), then
+  \[
+    \lvert\gamma\rvert=\beta\ \Longrightarrow\ \gamma^h=\rho,
+    \qquad
+    \lvert\gamma\rvert<\beta\ \Longrightarrow\
+      \lvert\gamma^h\rvert<\rho.
+  \]
+  In particular, every peripheral phase \(\gamma/\beta\) is an
+  \(h\)-th root of unity; the conclusion is stronger than merely placing
+  \(\gamma^h\) somewhere on the circle of radius \(\rho\).
+
+  \emph{Tail coefficients and their covariance.}
+  Put \(d=\deg\mu_U\), let \(K\) be a splitting field of \(\mu_U\), and
+  let \(J_{\mathrm r}\) be the threshold from which \(\mu_U\) annihilates
+  \(U\). The irreducible polynomial \(\mu_U\in\mathbb Q[X]\) is
+  separable. Hence there are unique coefficients \(A_\gamma\in K\), one
+  for each conjugate \(\gamma\) of \(\beta\), such that
+  \[
+    U_n=\sum_\gamma A_\gamma\gamma^n
+    \qquad(n\ge J_{\mathrm r}).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-tail-expansion}
+  \]
+  Indeed, the coefficients are determined by the \(d\) values with
+  \(n=J_{\mathrm r},\ldots,J_{\mathrm r}+d-1\); the corresponding matrix
+  is a nonsingular Vandermonde matrix multiplied by the nonzero diagonal
+  matrix \(\operatorname{diag}(\gamma^{J_{\mathrm r}})\). No polynomial
+  factors in \(n\) occur because every root is simple.
+
+  For \(\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(K/\mathbb Q)\), applying \(\sigma\)
+  to \eqref{eq:weak-perron-tail-expansion} and using
+  \(U_n\in\mathbb Q\) gives
+  \[
+    U_n=\sum_\gamma \sigma(A_\gamma)\sigma(\gamma)^n.
+  \]
+  Uniqueness of the expansion therefore yields the explicit covariance
+  identity
+  \[
+    A_{\sigma(\gamma)}=\sigma(A_\gamma).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-galois-covariance}
+  \]
+  For each conjugate \(\gamma\), the embedding
+  \(\mathbb Q(\beta)\hookrightarrow K\) that sends \(\beta\) to
+  \(\gamma\) extends to an automorphism of the splitting field \(K\).
+  Thus, if \(A_\beta=0\),
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-galois-covariance} forces every \(A_\gamma\) to vanish,
+  contradicting the positive, nonzero tail of \(U\). Consequently
+  \(A_\beta\ne0\); the same argument in fact shows that every
+  \(A_\gamma\ne0\).
+
+  \emph{Residue asymptotics.}
+  For each \(r\in\{0,\ldots,h-1\}\), set
+  \[
+    N_r:=\max\!\left\{0,
+      \left\lceil\frac{J_{\mathrm r}-r}{h}\right\rceil\right\},
+    \qquad
+    C_r:=\sum_{\lvert\gamma\rvert=\beta}A_\gamma\gamma^r.
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-residue-threshold-coefficient}
+  \]
+  Then \(hn+r\ge J_{\mathrm r}\) whenever \(n\ge N_r\), so
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-tail-expansion} applies. For a peripheral conjugate,
+  \(\gamma^{hn+r}=\gamma^r\rho^n\).
+  If \(\lvert\gamma\rvert<\beta\), then
+  \(\lvert\gamma^h\rvert<\rho\). If such conjugates exist, their total
+  contribution is \(O(\theta^n)\), where
+  \(\theta=\max_{\lvert\gamma\rvert<\beta}\lvert\gamma\rvert^h<\rho\);
+  if none exist, that contribution is identically zero and we choose any
+  \(0<\theta<\rho\). Therefore, for
+  every fixed residue \(r\),
+  \[
+    U_{hn+r}=C_r\rho^n+O(\theta^n)
+             =C_r\rho^n+o(\rho^n)
+    \qquad(n\ge N_r).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-residue-asymptotic}
+  \]
+  In particular,
+  \[
+    C_r=\lim_{n\to\infty}\rho^{-n}U_{hn+r}.
+  \]
+  The right-hand side is a limit of real nonnegative numbers, so
+  \(C_r\in\mathbb R\) and \(C_r\ge0\).
+
+  At least one residue coefficient is nonzero. To see this without any
+  suppressed independence argument, list the peripheral conjugates as
+  \(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_s\), and write
+  \(\gamma_j=\beta\zeta_j\). The \(\zeta_j\) are distinct \(h\)-th
+  roots of unity, so \(s\le h\). If \(C_r=0\) for every
+  \(0\le r<h\), then
+  \[
+    0=\beta^{-r}C_r
+      =\sum_{j=1}^s A_{\gamma_j}\zeta_j^r
+      \qquad(0\le r<h).
+      \label{eq:weak-perron-fourier-system}
+  \]
+  The \(h\times s\) Fourier--Vandermonde matrix
+  \[
+    (\zeta_j^r)_{\substack{0\le r<h\\1\le j\le s}}
+  \]
+  has full column rank: its first \(s\) rows form a square Vandermonde
+  matrix with determinant
+  \(\prod_{1\le i<j\le s}(\zeta_j-\zeta_i)\ne0\).
+  Equation \eqref{eq:weak-perron-fourier-system} would force all
+  peripheral coefficients to vanish,
+  including \(A_\beta\), a contradiction.
+
+  \emph{Cyclic propagation of positivity.}
+  Choose \(r\) with \(C_r>0\). If \(r<h-1\), then for all sufficiently
+  large \(n\), strict increase gives
+  \[
+    U_{hn+r}<U_{hn+r+1}.
+  \]
+  Divide by \(\rho^n\) and use
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-residue-asymptotic} for both residue classes. The
+  limiting inequality gives \(C_r\le C_{r+1}\), so in particular
+  \(C_{r+1}>0\). At the wraparound, strict increase gives
+  \[
+    U_{hn+h-1}<U_{h(n+1)},
+    \qquad
+    \rho^{-n}U_{h(n+1)}\longrightarrow\rho C_0,
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-wraparound-limit}
+  \]
+  whereas \(\rho^{-n}U_{hn+h-1}\to C_{h-1}\). Thus
+  \(C_{h-1}\le\rho C_0\), and \(C_{h-1}>0\) forces \(C_0>0\).
+  Starting from one positive coefficient and moving cyclically proves
+  \[
+    C_r>0\qquad(0\le r<h).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-positive-residues}
+  \]
+
+  Finally, if \(N=hn+r\), then
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-residue-asymptotic} and
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-positive-residues} give
+  \begin{align*}
+    U_N&=C_r\rho^n(1+o(1)),\\
+    \frac{\log U_N}{N}
+      &=\frac{n\log\rho+\log C_r+o(1)}{hn+r}
+        \longrightarrow\frac{\log\rho}{h}=\log\beta.
+  \end{align*}
+  There are only finitely many residues, so this proves the global limit
+  \[
+    \lim_{N\to\infty}U_N^{1/N}=\beta.
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-global-root-limit}
+  \]

+\paragraph{Greedy length interval.}
+For a standard greedy linear numeration basis with \(U_0=1\), a positive

+in the half-open interval

+  We first establish the asymptotic needed for
+  \textup{(ii)}\(\Rightarrow\)\textup{(iii)}. This conclusion is also
+  obtainable from Charlier--Kreczman's quotient-limit mechanism
+  \cite[Proposition~10 and Remark~12]{CharlierKreczman2025}; we give the
+  coefficient-level argument because the residue thresholds and positivity
+  are part of the hypotheses used here.
+
+  \emph{Peripheral period.}
+  The classical power characterization of weak Perron numbers gives an
+  integer \(h\ge1\) for which
+  \[
+    \rho:=\beta^h
+  \]
+  is a Perron number \cite{Brunotte2013,Lind1984}. Equivalently, if
+  \(\gamma\) is any conjugate of \(\beta\), then
+  \[
+    \lvert\gamma\rvert=\beta\ \Longrightarrow\ \gamma^h=\rho,
+    \qquad
+    \lvert\gamma\rvert<\beta\ \Longrightarrow\
+      \lvert\gamma^h\rvert<\rho.
+  \]
+  In particular, every peripheral phase \(\gamma/\beta\) is an
+  \(h\)-th root of unity; the conclusion is stronger than merely placing
+  \(\gamma^h\) somewhere on the circle of radius \(\rho\).
+
+  \emph{Tail coefficients and their covariance.}
+  Put \(d=\deg\mu_U\), let \(K\) be a splitting field of \(\mu_U\), and
+  let \(J_{\mathrm r}\) be the threshold from which \(\mu_U\) annihilates
+  \(U\). The irreducible polynomial \(\mu_U\in\mathbb Q[X]\) is
+  separable. Hence there are unique coefficients \(A_\gamma\in K\), one
+  for each conjugate \(\gamma\) of \(\beta\), such that
+  \[
+    U_n=\sum_\gamma A_\gamma\gamma^n
+    \qquad(n\ge J_{\mathrm r}).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-tail-expansion}
+  \]
+  Indeed, the coefficients are determined by the \(d\) values with
+  \(n=J_{\mathrm r},\ldots,J_{\mathrm r}+d-1\); the corresponding matrix
+  is a nonsingular Vandermonde matrix multiplied by the nonzero diagonal
+  matrix \(\operatorname{diag}(\gamma^{J_{\mathrm r}})\). No polynomial
+  factors in \(n\) occur because every root is simple.
+
+  For \(\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(K/\mathbb Q)\), applying \(\sigma\)
+  to \eqref{eq:weak-perron-tail-expansion} and using
+  \(U_n\in\mathbb Q\) gives
+  \[
+    U_n=\sum_\gamma \sigma(A_\gamma)\sigma(\gamma)^n.
+  \]
+  Uniqueness of the expansion therefore yields the explicit covariance
+  identity
+  \[
+    A_{\sigma(\gamma)}=\sigma(A_\gamma).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-galois-covariance}
+  \]
+  For each conjugate \(\gamma\), the embedding
+  \(\mathbb Q(\beta)\hookrightarrow K\) that sends \(\beta\) to
+  \(\gamma\) extends to an automorphism of the splitting field \(K\).
+  Thus, if \(A_\beta=0\),
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-galois-covariance} forces every \(A_\gamma\) to vanish,
+  contradicting the positive, nonzero tail of \(U\). Consequently
+  \(A_\beta\ne0\); the same argument in fact shows that every
+  \(A_\gamma\ne0\).
+
+  \emph{Residue asymptotics.}
+  For each \(r\in\{0,\ldots,h-1\}\), set
+  \[
+    N_r:=\max\!\left\{0,
+      \left\lceil\frac{J_{\mathrm r}-r}{h}\right\rceil\right\},
+    \qquad
+    C_r:=\sum_{\lvert\gamma\rvert=\beta}A_\gamma\gamma^r.
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-residue-threshold-coefficient}
+  \]
+  Then \(hn+r\ge J_{\mathrm r}\) whenever \(n\ge N_r\), so
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-tail-expansion} applies. For a peripheral conjugate,
+  \(\gamma^{hn+r}=\gamma^r\rho^n\).
+  If \(\lvert\gamma\rvert<\beta\), then
+  \(\lvert\gamma^h\rvert<\rho\). If such conjugates exist, their total
+  contribution is \(O(\theta^n)\), where
+  \(\theta=\max_{\lvert\gamma\rvert<\beta}\lvert\gamma\rvert^h<\rho\);
+  if none exist, that contribution is identically zero and we choose any
+  \(0<\theta<\rho\). Therefore, for
+  every fixed residue \(r\),
+  \[
+    U_{hn+r}=C_r\rho^n+O(\theta^n)
+             =C_r\rho^n+o(\rho^n)
+    \qquad(n\ge N_r).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-residue-asymptotic}
+  \]
+  In particular,
+  \[
+    C_r=\lim_{n\to\infty}\rho^{-n}U_{hn+r}.
+  \]
+  The right-hand side is a limit of real nonnegative numbers, so
+  \(C_r\in\mathbb R\) and \(C_r\ge0\).
+
+  At least one residue coefficient is nonzero. To see this without any
+  suppressed independence argument, list the peripheral conjugates as
+  \(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_s\), and write
+  \(\gamma_j=\beta\zeta_j\). The \(\zeta_j\) are distinct \(h\)-th
+  roots of unity, so \(s\le h\). If \(C_r=0\) for every
+  \(0\le r<h\), then
+  \[
+    0=\beta^{-r}C_r
+      =\sum_{j=1}^s A_{\gamma_j}\zeta_j^r
+      \qquad(0\le r<h).
+      \label{eq:weak-perron-fourier-system}
+  \]
+  The \(h\times s\) Fourier--Vandermonde matrix
+  \[
+    (\zeta_j^r)_{\substack{0\le r<h\\1\le j\le s}}
+  \]
+  has full column rank: its first \(s\) rows form a square Vandermonde
+  matrix with determinant
+  \(\prod_{1\le i<j\le s}(\zeta_j-\zeta_i)\ne0\).
+  Equation \eqref{eq:weak-perron-fourier-system} would force all
+  peripheral coefficients to vanish,
+  including \(A_\beta\), a contradiction.
+
+  \emph{Cyclic propagation of positivity.}
+  Choose \(r\) with \(C_r>0\). If \(r<h-1\), then for all sufficiently
+  large \(n\), strict increase gives
+  \[
+    U_{hn+r}<U_{hn+r+1}.
+  \]
+  Divide by \(\rho^n\) and use
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-residue-asymptotic} for both residue classes. The
+  limiting inequality gives \(C_r\le C_{r+1}\), so in particular
+  \(C_{r+1}>0\). At the wraparound, strict increase gives
+  \[
+    U_{hn+h-1}<U_{h(n+1)},
+    \qquad
+    \rho^{-n}U_{h(n+1)}\longrightarrow\rho C_0,
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-wraparound-limit}
+  \]
+  whereas \(\rho^{-n}U_{hn+h-1}\to C_{h-1}\). Thus
+  \(C_{h-1}\le\rho C_0\), and \(C_{h-1}>0\) forces \(C_0>0\).
+  Starting from one positive coefficient and moving cyclically proves
+  \[
+    C_r>0\qquad(0\le r<h).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-positive-residues}
+  \]
+
+  Finally, if \(N=hn+r\), then
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-residue-asymptotic} and
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-positive-residues} give
+  \begin{align*}
+    U_N&=C_r\rho^n(1+o(1)),\\
+    \frac{\log U_N}{N}
+      &=\frac{n\log\rho+\log C_r+o(1)}{hn+r}
+        \longrightarrow\frac{\log\rho}{h}=\log\beta.
+  \end{align*}
+  There are only finitely many residues, so this proves the global limit
+  \[
+    \lim_{N\to\infty}U_N^{1/N}=\beta.
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-global-root-limit}
+  \]

exec

+Charlier--Kreczman remove the dominant-root restriction from the regularity
+problem for positional numeration systems \cite{CharlierKreczman2025}.
+They associate a periodic alternate real base to the residue classes of the
+place-value sequence and give a full characterization of regularity through
+the graph of the greedy and quasi-greedy expansions of (1) in the shifted
+alternate bases. Their procedure is a semidecision in general, and becomes a
+decision procedure when the associated alternate base is known to be Parry.
+Their Proposition~10 proves that regularity of the whole greedy language
+forces residue-class consecutive-quotient limits. More directly relevant
+here, Remark~12 states that, for an arbitrary linear recurrence, equality of
+the (p)-th powers of its dominating eigenvalues implies convergence of
+\(U_n/U_{n-p}\) to that common power when \((\lvert U_n\rvert)\) is
+eventually increasing. Under the irreducible weak-Perron hypotheses below,
+separability gives equal peripheral multiplicities, weak-Perron periodicity
+gives the common power, and strict increase supplies their last hypothesis.
+Thus their work already contains the root-growth mechanism needed for our
+length squeeze, in essentially equivalent quotient-limit form. We retain a
+self-contained coefficient-level proof because it identifies every residue
+coefficient and verifies positivity under exactly our hypotheses. Their
+regularity characterization neither assumes nor concludes anything about
+MCFL sublanguages, bounded prime support, synchronized geometric schemes, or
+the five equivalent conditions proved here; conversely, our theorem does not
+characterize regularity of the whole greedy language.

+\paragraph{Greedy length interval.}
+For a standard greedy linear numeration basis with \(U_0=1\), a positive
+integer has a canonical greedy word of length \(m\) if and only if it lies
+in the half-open interval
+\[
+  [U_{m-1},U_m).
+\]
+Indeed, the greedy algorithm chooses the least threshold \(U_m\) strictly
+larger than the represented integer; minimality of \(m\) gives the lower
+bound, and the choice of \(U_m\) gives the upper bound. This is a property
+of the standard greedy subclass, not an assumption on the ambient
+canonical eventually recurrent systems.

+  We first establish the asymptotic needed for
+  \textup{(ii)}\(\Rightarrow\)\textup{(iii)}. This conclusion is also
+  obtainable from Charlier--Kreczman's quotient-limit mechanism
+  \cite[Proposition~10 and Remark~12]{CharlierKreczman2025}; we give the
+  coefficient-level argument because the residue thresholds and positivity
+  are part of the hypotheses used here.
+
+  \emph{Peripheral period.}
+  The classical power characterization of weak Perron numbers gives an
+  integer \(h\ge1\) for which
+  \[
+    \rho:=\beta^h
+  \]
+  is a Perron number \cite{Brunotte2013,Lind1984}. Equivalently, if
+  \(\gamma\) is any conjugate of \(\beta\), then
+  \[
+    \lvert\gamma\rvert=\beta\ \Longrightarrow\ \gamma^h=\rho,
+    \qquad
+    \lvert\gamma\rvert<\beta\ \Longrightarrow\
+      \lvert\gamma^h\rvert<\rho.
+  \]
+  In particular, every peripheral phase \(\gamma/\beta\) is an
+  \(h\)-th root of unity; the conclusion is stronger than merely placing
+  \(\gamma^h\) somewhere on the circle of radius \(\rho\).
+
+  \emph{Tail coefficients and their covariance.}
+  Put \(d=\deg\mu_U\), let \(K\) be a splitting field of \(\mu_U\), and
+  let \(J_{\mathrm r}\) be the threshold from which \(\mu_U\) annihilates
+  \(U\). The irreducible polynomial \(\mu_U\in\mathbb Q[X]\) is
+  separable. Hence there are unique coefficients \(A_\gamma\in K\), one
+  for each conjugate \(\gamma\) of \(\beta\), such that
+  \[
+    U_n=\sum_\gamma A_\gamma\gamma^n
+    \qquad(n\ge J_{\mathrm r}).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-tail-expansion}
+  \]
+  Indeed, the coefficients are determined by the \(d\) values with
+  \(n=J_{\mathrm r},\ldots,J_{\mathrm r}+d-1\); the corresponding matrix
+  is a nonsingular Vandermonde matrix multiplied by the nonzero diagonal
+  matrix \(\operatorname{diag}(\gamma^{J_{\mathrm r}})\). No polynomial
+  factors in \(n\) occur because every root is simple.
+
+  For \(\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(K/\mathbb Q)\), applying \(\sigma\)
+  to \eqref{eq:weak-perron-tail-expansion} and using
+  \(U_n\in\mathbb Q\) gives
+  \[
+    U_n=\sum_\gamma \sigma(A_\gamma)\sigma(\gamma)^n.
+  \]
+  Uniqueness of the expansion therefore yields the explicit covariance
+  identity
+  \[
+    A_{\sigma(\gamma)}=\sigma(A_\gamma).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-galois-covariance}
+  \]
+  For each conjugate \(\gamma\), the embedding
+  \(\mathbb Q(\beta)\hookrightarrow K\) that sends \(\beta\) to
+  \(\gamma\) extends to an automorphism of the splitting field \(K\).
+  Thus, if \(A_\beta=0\),
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-galois-covariance} forces every \(A_\gamma\) to vanish,
+  contradicting the positive, nonzero tail of \(U\). Consequently
+  \(A_\beta\ne0\); the same argument in fact shows that every
+  \(A_\gamma\ne0\).
+
+  \emph{Residue asymptotics.}
+  For each \(r\in\{0,\ldots,h-1\}\), set
+  \[
+    N_r:=\max\!\left\{0,
+      \left\lceil\frac{J_{\mathrm r}-r}{h}\right\rceil\right\},
+    \qquad
+    C_r:=\sum_{\lvert\gamma\rvert=\beta}A_\gamma\gamma^r.
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-residue-threshold-coefficient}
+  \]
+  Then \(hn+r\ge J_{\mathrm r}\) whenever \(n\ge N_r\), so
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-tail-expansion} applies. For a peripheral conjugate,
+  \(\gamma^{hn+r}=\gamma^r\rho^n\).
+  If \(\lvert\gamma\rvert<\beta\), then
+  \(\lvert\gamma^h\rvert<\rho\). If such conjugates exist, their total
+  contribution is \(O(\theta^n)\), where
+  \(\theta=\max_{\lvert\gamma\rvert<\beta}\lvert\gamma\rvert^h<\rho\);
+  if none exist, that contribution is identically zero and we choose any
+  \(0<\theta<\rho\). Therefore, for
+  every fixed residue \(r\),
+  \[
+    U_{hn+r}=C_r\rho^n+O(\theta^n)
+             =C_r\rho^n+o(\rho^n)
+    \qquad(n\ge N_r).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-residue-asymptotic}
+  \]
+  In particular,
+  \[
+    C_r=\lim_{n\to\infty}\rho^{-n}U_{hn+r}.
+  \]
+  The right-hand side is a limit of real nonnegative numbers, so
+  \(C_r\in\mathbb R\) and \(C_r\ge0\).
+
+  At least one residue coefficient is nonzero. To see this without any
+  suppressed independence argument, list the peripheral conjugates as
+  \(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_s\), and write
+  \(\gamma_j=\beta\zeta_j\). The \(\zeta_j\) are distinct \(h\)-th
+  roots of unity, so \(s\le h\). If \(C_r=0\) for every
+  \(0\le r<h\), then
+  \[
+    0=\beta^{-r}C_r
+      =\sum_{j=1}^s A_{\gamma_j}\zeta_j^r
+      \qquad(0\le r<h).
+      \label{eq:weak-perron-fourier-system}
+  \]
+  The \(h\times s\) Fourier--Vandermonde matrix
+  \[
+    (\zeta_j^r)_{\substack{0\le r<h\\1\le j\le s}}
+  \]
+  has full column rank: its first \(s\) rows form a square Vandermonde
+  matrix with determinant
+  \(\prod_{1\le i<j\le s}(\zeta_j-\zeta_i)\ne0\).
+  Equation \eqref{eq:weak-perron-fourier-system} would force all
+  peripheral coefficients to vanish,
+  including \(A_\beta\), a contradiction.
+
+  \emph{Cyclic propagation of positivity.}
+  Choose \(r\) with \(C_r>0\). If \(r<h-1\), then for all sufficiently
+  large \(n\), strict increase gives
+  \[
+    U_{hn+r}<U_{hn+r+1}.
+  \]
+  Divide by \(\rho^n\) and use
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-residue-asymptotic} for both residue classes. The
+  limiting inequality gives \(C_r\le C_{r+1}\), so in particular
+  \(C_{r+1}>0\). At the wraparound, strict increase gives
+  \[
+    U_{hn+h-1}<U_{h(n+1)},
+    \qquad
+    \rho^{-n}U_{h(n+1)}\longrightarrow\rho C_0,
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-wraparound-limit}
+  \]
+  whereas \(\rho^{-n}U_{hn+h-1}\to C_{h-1}\). Thus
+  \(C_{h-1}\le\rho C_0\), and \(C_{h-1}>0\) forces \(C_0>0\).
+  Starting from one positive coefficient and moving cyclically proves
+  \[
+    C_r>0\qquad(0\le r<h).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-positive-residues}
+  \]
+
+  Finally, if \(N=hn+r\), then
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-residue-asymptotic} and
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-positive-residues} give
+  \begin{align*}
+    U_N&=C_r\rho^n(1+o(1)),\\
+    \frac{\log U_N}{N}
+      &=\frac{n\log\rho+\log C_r+o(1)}{hn+r}
+        \longrightarrow\frac{\log\rho}{h}=\log\beta.
+  \end{align*}
+  There are only finitely many residues, so this proves the global limit
+  \[
+    \lim_{N\to\infty}U_N^{1/N}=\beta.
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-global-root-limit}
+  \]

20  HAOBO MA AND WENLIN ZHANG

Greedy length interval. For a standard greedy linear numeration basis with
U0 = 1, a positive integer has a canonical greedy word of length m if and
only if it lies in the half-open interval

                                         [Um-1, Um).

Indeed, the greedy algorithm chooses the least threshold Um strictly larger
than the represented integer; minimality of m gives the lower bound, and
the choice of Um gives the upper bound. This is a property of the standard
greedy subclass, not an assumption on the ambient canonical eventually
recurrent systems.

Corollary 2.23 (Linear numeration bases with Perron recurrence). Let
U = (Un)n0 be a standard greedy linear numeration basis in the following
precise sense: U0 = 1, the Un are strictly increasing integers with bounded
quotients, RU is the LSD-first reversal of the usual greedy representation
language, and U has minimal tail recurrence polynomial equal to the minimal
polynomial of a Perron number . Thus  > 1 is a real algebraic integer
and every other conjugate  satisfies || < ; compare [51, 64]. Then its
prime representation language is MCF-immune, hence CF-immune, REG-
immune and nonrecognizable. The same statements hold in the usual MSD-
first convention.

   If the dominant Perron number is a unit and the chosen recurrence has
trailing coefficient a0 = �1, then the full coprime-quotient and bounded-
prime-support MCF-immunity conclusions of Theorem 2.22 hold.

Proof. Greedy expansion gives a unique representation of every positive inte-

ger, and its length-m words represent values between successive place-value

thresholds; thus (U1) and (U2) hold. The defining Perron recurrence gives

(U4). Apply Theorem 2.22. The immunity proof uses only (U1), (U2),

and (U4) and does not assume that the full greedy language is regular. In

the Pisot subclass, Frougny's finite normalization theorem supplies a finite

transducer, and the associated canonical syntax and Bertrand/substitution

descriptions are standard [38, 14, 36, 39]. Finally, multiple context-free,

context-free, and regular languages are closed under reversal, so changing

between the LSD-first proof convention and the usual MSD-first convention

preserves every conclusion.                        

Example 2.24 (Pisot and non-Pisot Perron systems). The Fibonacci re-
currence has characteristic polynomial X2 - X - 1, the Pell recurrence has
X2 - 2X - 1, and the Tribonacci recurrence has X3 - X2 - X - 1. Their
trailing recurrence coefficient is a0 = 1, so the iterated conclusion applies. In
ordinary base b, Un = bn and a0 = b; prime MCF-immunity follows, strength-
ening the classical fixed-base CF-immunity conclusion to MCF-immunity,

but the unit iteration is not being asserted.

   There is also an infinite family of genuinely nonintegral weak-Perron sys-

tems. Let p, q  2, put B = pq, and suppose that B is not a square. Define

    U2t = Bt,                U2t+1 = pBt  (t  0).

The successive quotients are alternately p and q. Repeated Euclidean divi-
sion in these alternating radices gives every positive integer a unique greedy
expansion: the digit at an even position lies in {0, . . . , p - 1}, and the digit
PRIME SUPPORT IN RECURRENT NUMERATION                                21

at an odd position lies in {0, . . . , q - 1}. Hence the LSD-first canonical lan-
guage is regular, since a finite automaton need only track position parity,
the relevant digit bound, and a nonzero final digit. Moreover,

                                         Un+2 = BUn,

and the irreducible polynomial X2 -B is the minimal recurrence polynomial.
Its positive root B is nonintegral and weak Perron, with conjugate - B
of the same modulus. The regular ray {02t1 : t  0} has values Bt. Thus
p = 2, q = 3 gives the sequence 1, 2, 6, 12, 36, 72, . . ., while p = 2, q = 5 gives
a second concrete member 1, 2, 10, 20, 100, 200, . . ..

   A genuinely nonintegral, nonunit Pisot example is obtained from

U0 = 1, U1 = 3, Un+2 = 2Un+1 + 2Un.

If 2 < Un+1/Un  3, then

Un+2 = 2 + 2Un  [8/3, 3),
Un+1                               Un+1

so induction from U1/U0 = 3 proves strict increase and bounded quotients.
The irreducible polynomial X2 - 2X - 2 annihilates this nonzero rational
sequence, hence is its minimal tail polynomial. Its dominant root is 1 + 3,

and its trailing coefficient is a0 = 2, so the action is singular modulo 2. Nev-
ertheless, Theorem 2.25 shows that every infinite MCFL in this nonintegral

system acquires unbounded prime support away from 2; singularity of the

Remark 2.26 (Exact open interfaces). The terminology for linear numera-
tion systems with Perron or Pisot recurrence is not uniform. Corollary 2.23
covers the standard positional linear U -systems just specified, including in-
teger bases, Zeckendorf/Fibonacci, Pell, higher-order Pisot recurrences, and
non-Pisot Perron examples such as X2 - 5X + 5. It does not assert the the-
orem for arbitrary real-base -shift representations, non-positional abstract
numeration systems, redundant noninjective digit systems, or systems lack-
ing an eventual integral recurrence. Extending the argument to any of those
classes requires a stationary finite block action that is invertible modulo
represented primes.

   For a fixed nonunit recurrence witness, the ambient action can be singular
modulo primes dividing a0, so the unrestricted unit-system divisibility tree
need not follow. The witness-relative surviving statement is Theorem 2.11:
every infinite MCFL must acquire unbounded prime support outside that
finite set or unbounded valuation at one of its primes. The invariant re-
stricted action and the failure of arbitrary recurrence witnesses to classify
escape behavior are distinguished in Proposition 2.12. Within greedy linear
numeration bases with weak-Perron recurrence, the residual alternative is
classified by Theorem 2.25: it occurs exactly when a positive power of the
weak Perron number is an integer. The ordinary-base example preceding
Theorem 2.20 shows that the valuation alternative cannot be removed.

3. Conclusion and open interface

The affine recurrence action turns one weak MCFL pumping family into

a single injective numerical orbit with simultaneous local returns. Posi-

tive pumped length and uniqueness of canonical representation supply dis-

tinctness, while finite-group return times supply congruences. Applying

Broughan's adic classifications to these orbits, together with the deleted-

prime intrinsic derivative calculation, gives the scattered-set obstruction,

the nonunit escape dichotomy, and prime and bounded- MCF-immunity.

For the minimal tail recurrence, the residual bounded-support phenom-

enon has an exact structural form. It occurs on an infinite finite-fan-out

MCFL if and only if the canonical language contains a synchronized ray

with values cbt. Evertse's quotient theorem is used with an explicit prime-

ideal norm bound to reduce a fixed-support recurrence to one characteristic

root; Schur's theorem removes its polynomial factor. The ratio b uses only

primes dividing the minimal tail constant. In a standard greedy linear nu-

meration basis with weak-Perron recurrence, residue asymptotics and length

thresholds show that such a ray exists exactly when some positive power of

the weak Perron number is an integer.  Alternating radices give   an  infinite
family with nonintegral root B and a   regular ray of values Bt.

On the promised class of valid effectively presented regular canonical sys-

tems, with the minimal tail recurrence and threshold supplied or certified,

positive promised instances can be enumerated and certified. The unre-

solved general step is not candidate verification but witness compression: no

computable bound is known for the fan-out and word lengths of a smallest

geometric synchronized scheme. DFA path compression does not preserve

the associated affine recurrence matrices. Conversely, no reduction proving

+\paragraph{Greedy length interval.}
+For a standard greedy linear numeration basis with \(U_0=1\), a positive
+integer has a canonical greedy word of length \(m\) if and only if it lies
+in the half-open interval
+\[

+of the standard greedy subclass, not an assumption on the ambient
+canonical eventually recurrent systems.

+  We first establish the asymptotic needed for
+  \textup{(ii)}\(\Rightarrow\)\textup{(iii)}. This conclusion is also
+  obtainable from Charlier--Kreczman's quotient-limit mechanism
+  \cite[Proposition~10 and Remark~12]{CharlierKreczman2025}; we give the
+  coefficient-level argument because the residue thresholds and positivity
+  are part of the hypotheses used here.
+
+  \emph{Peripheral period.}
+  The classical power characterization of weak Perron numbers gives an
+  integer \(h\ge1\) for which
+  \[
+    \rho:=\beta^h
+  \]
+  is a Perron number \cite{Brunotte2013,Lind1984}. Equivalently, if
+  \(\gamma\) is any conjugate of \(\beta\), then
+  \[
+    \lvert\gamma\rvert=\beta\ \Longrightarrow\ \gamma^h=\rho,
+    \qquad
+    \lvert\gamma\rvert<\beta\ \Longrightarrow\
+      \lvert\gamma^h\rvert<\rho.
+  \]
+  In particular, every peripheral phase \(\gamma/\beta\) is an
+  \(h\)-th root of unity; the conclusion is stronger than merely placing
+  \(\gamma^h\) somewhere on the circle of radius \(\rho\).
+
+  \emph{Tail coefficients and their covariance.}
+  Put \(d=\deg\mu_U\), let \(K\) be a splitting field of \(\mu_U\), and
+  let \(J_{\mathrm r}\) be the threshold from which \(\mu_U\) annihilates
+  \(U\). The irreducible polynomial \(\mu_U\in\mathbb Q[X]\) is
+  separable. Hence there are unique coefficients \(A_\gamma\in K\), one
+  for each conjugate \(\gamma\) of \(\beta\), such that
+  \[
+    U_n=\sum_\gamma A_\gamma\gamma^n
+    \qquad(n\ge J_{\mathrm r}).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-tail-expansion}
+  \]
+  Indeed, the coefficients are determined by the \(d\) values with
+  \(n=J_{\mathrm r},\ldots,J_{\mathrm r}+d-1\); the corresponding matrix
+  is a nonsingular Vandermonde matrix multiplied by the nonzero diagonal
+  matrix \(\operatorname{diag}(\gamma^{J_{\mathrm r}})\). No polynomial
+  factors in \(n\) occur because every root is simple.
+
+  For \(\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(K/\mathbb Q)\), applying \(\sigma\)
+  to \eqref{eq:weak-perron-tail-expansion} and using
+  \(U_n\in\mathbb Q\) gives
+  \[
+    U_n=\sum_\gamma \sigma(A_\gamma)\sigma(\gamma)^n.
+  \]
+  Uniqueness of the expansion therefore yields the explicit covariance
+  identity
+  \[
+    A_{\sigma(\gamma)}=\sigma(A_\gamma).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-galois-covariance}
+  \]
+  For each conjugate \(\gamma\), the embedding
+  \(\mathbb Q(\beta)\hookrightarrow K\) that sends \(\beta\) to
+  \(\gamma\) extends to an automorphism of the splitting field \(K\).
+  Thus, if \(A_\beta=0\),
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-galois-covariance} forces every \(A_\gamma\) to vanish,
+  contradicting the positive, nonzero tail of \(U\). Consequently
+  \(A_\beta\ne0\); the same argument in fact shows that every
+  \(A_\gamma\ne0\).
+
+  \emph{Residue asymptotics.}
+  For each \(r\in\{0,\ldots,h-1\}\), set
+  \[
+    N_r:=\max\!\left\{0,
+      \left\lceil\frac{J_{\mathrm r}-r}{h}\right\rceil\right\},
+    \qquad
+    C_r:=\sum_{\lvert\gamma\rvert=\beta}A_\gamma\gamma^r.
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-residue-threshold-coefficient}
+  \]
+  Then \(hn+r\ge J_{\mathrm r}\) whenever \(n\ge N_r\), so
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-tail-expansion} applies. For a peripheral conjugate,
+  \(\gamma^{hn+r}=\gamma^r\rho^n\).
+  If \(\lvert\gamma\rvert<\beta\), then
+  \(\lvert\gamma^h\rvert<\rho\). If such conjugates exist, their total
+  contribution is \(O(\theta^n)\), where
+  \(\theta=\max_{\lvert\gamma\rvert<\beta}\lvert\gamma\rvert^h<\rho\);
+  if none exist, that contribution is identically zero and we choose any
+  \(0<\theta<\rho\). Therefore, for
+  every fixed residue \(r\),
+  \[
+    U_{hn+r}=C_r\rho^n+O(\theta^n)
+             =C_r\rho^n+o(\rho^n)
+    \qquad(n\ge N_r).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-residue-asymptotic}
+  \]
+  In particular,
+  \[
+    C_r=\lim_{n\to\infty}\rho^{-n}U_{hn+r}.
+  \]
+  The right-hand side is a limit of real nonnegative numbers, so
+  \(C_r\in\mathbb R\) and \(C_r\ge0\).
+
+  At least one residue coefficient is nonzero. To see this without any
+  suppressed independence argument, list the peripheral conjugates as
+  \(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_s\), and write
+  \(\gamma_j=\beta\zeta_j\). The \(\zeta_j\) are distinct \(h\)-th
+  roots of unity, so \(s\le h\). If \(C_r=0\) for every
+  \(0\le r<h\), then
+  \[
+    0=\beta^{-r}C_r
+      =\sum_{j=1}^s A_{\gamma_j}\zeta_j^r
+      \qquad(0\le r<h).
+      \label{eq:weak-perron-fourier-system}
+  \]
+  The \(h\times s\) Fourier--Vandermonde matrix
+  \[
+    (\zeta_j^r)_{\substack{0\le r<h\\1\le j\le s}}
+  \]
+  has full column rank: its first \(s\) rows form a square Vandermonde
+  matrix with determinant
+  \(\prod_{1\le i<j\le s}(\zeta_j-\zeta_i)\ne0\).
+  Equation \eqref{eq:weak-perron-fourier-system} would force all
+  peripheral coefficients to vanish,
+  including \(A_\beta\), a contradiction.
+
+  \emph{Cyclic propagation of positivity.}
+  Choose \(r\) with \(C_r>0\). If \(r<h-1\), then for all sufficiently
+  large \(n\), strict increase gives
+  \[
+    U_{hn+r}<U_{hn+r+1}.
+  \]
+  Divide by \(\rho^n\) and use
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-residue-asymptotic} for both residue classes. The
+  limiting inequality gives \(C_r\le C_{r+1}\), so in particular
+  \(C_{r+1}>0\). At the wraparound, strict increase gives
+  \[
+    U_{hn+h-1}<U_{h(n+1)},
+    \qquad
+    \rho^{-n}U_{h(n+1)}\longrightarrow\rho C_0,
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-wraparound-limit}
+  \]
+  whereas \(\rho^{-n}U_{hn+h-1}\to C_{h-1}\). Thus
+  \(C_{h-1}\le\rho C_0\), and \(C_{h-1}>0\) forces \(C_0>0\).
+  Starting from one positive coefficient and moving cyclically proves
+  \[
+    C_r>0\qquad(0\le r<h).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-positive-residues}
+  \]
+
+  Finally, if \(N=hn+r\), then
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-residue-asymptotic} and
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-positive-residues} give
+  \begin{align*}
+    U_N&=C_r\rho^n(1+o(1)),\\
+    \frac{\log U_N}{N}
+      &=\frac{n\log\rho+\log C_r+o(1)}{hn+r}
+        \longrightarrow\frac{\log\rho}{h}=\log\beta.
+  \end{align*}
+  There are only finitely many residues, so this proves the global limit
+  \[
+    \lim_{N\to\infty}U_N^{1/N}=\beta.
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-global-root-limit}
+  \]

+\paragraph{Greedy length interval.}
+For a standard greedy linear numeration basis with \(U_0=1\), a positive
+integer has a canonical greedy word of length \(m\) if and only if it lies
+in the half-open interval
+\[

+bound, and the choice of \(U_m\) gives the upper bound. This is a property
+of the standard greedy subclass, not an assumption on the ambient
+canonical eventually recurrent systems.

+  We first establish the asymptotic needed for
+  \textup{(ii)}\(\Rightarrow\)\textup{(iii)}. This conclusion is also
+  obtainable from Charlier--Kreczman's quotient-limit mechanism
+  \cite[Proposition~10 and Remark~12]{CharlierKreczman2025}; we give the
+  coefficient-level argument because the residue thresholds and positivity
+  are part of the hypotheses used here.
+
+  \emph{Peripheral period.}
+  The classical power characterization of weak Perron numbers gives an
+  integer \(h\ge1\) for which
+  \[
+    \rho:=\beta^h
+  \]
+  is a Perron number \cite{Brunotte2013,Lind1984}. Equivalently, if
+  \(\gamma\) is any conjugate of \(\beta\), then
+  \[
+    \lvert\gamma\rvert=\beta\ \Longrightarrow\ \gamma^h=\rho,
+    \qquad
+    \lvert\gamma\rvert<\beta\ \Longrightarrow\
+      \lvert\gamma^h\rvert<\rho.
+  \]
+  In particular, every peripheral phase \(\gamma/\beta\) is an
+  \(h\)-th root of unity; the conclusion is stronger than merely placing
+  \(\gamma^h\) somewhere on the circle of radius \(\rho\).
+
+  \emph{Tail coefficients and their covariance.}
+  Put \(d=\deg\mu_U\), let \(K\) be a splitting field of \(\mu_U\), and
+  let \(J_{\mathrm r}\) be the threshold from which \(\mu_U\) annihilates
+  \(U\). The irreducible polynomial \(\mu_U\in\mathbb Q[X]\) is
+  separable. Hence there are unique coefficients \(A_\gamma\in K\), one
+  for each conjugate \(\gamma\) of \(\beta\), such that
+  \[
+    U_n=\sum_\gamma A_\gamma\gamma^n
+    \qquad(n\ge J_{\mathrm r}).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-tail-expansion}
+  \]
+  Indeed, the coefficients are determined by the \(d\) values with
+  \(n=J_{\mathrm r},\ldots,J_{\mathrm r}+d-1\); the corresponding matrix
+  is a nonsingular Vandermonde matrix multiplied by the nonzero diagonal
+  matrix \(\operatorname{diag}(\gamma^{J_{\mathrm r}})\). No polynomial
+  factors in \(n\) occur because every root is simple.
+
+  For \(\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(K/\mathbb Q)\), applying \(\sigma\)
+  to \eqref{eq:weak-perron-tail-expansion} and using
+  \(U_n\in\mathbb Q\) gives
+  \[
+    U_n=\sum_\gamma \sigma(A_\gamma)\sigma(\gamma)^n.
+  \]
+  Uniqueness of the expansion therefore yields the explicit covariance
+  identity
+  \[
+    A_{\sigma(\gamma)}=\sigma(A_\gamma).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-galois-covariance}
+  \]
+  For each conjugate \(\gamma\), the embedding
+  \(\mathbb Q(\beta)\hookrightarrow K\) that sends \(\beta\) to
+  \(\gamma\) extends to an automorphism of the splitting field \(K\).
+  Thus, if \(A_\beta=0\),
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-galois-covariance} forces every \(A_\gamma\) to vanish,
+  contradicting the positive, nonzero tail of \(U\). Consequently
+  \(A_\beta\ne0\); the same argument in fact shows that every
+  \(A_\gamma\ne0\).
+
+  \emph{Residue asymptotics.}
+  For each \(r\in\{0,\ldots,h-1\}\), set
+  \[
+    N_r:=\max\!\left\{0,
+      \left\lceil\frac{J_{\mathrm r}-r}{h}\right\rceil\right\},
+    \qquad
+    C_r:=\sum_{\lvert\gamma\rvert=\beta}A_\gamma\gamma^r.
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-residue-threshold-coefficient}
+  \]
+  Then \(hn+r\ge J_{\mathrm r}\) whenever \(n\ge N_r\), so
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-tail-expansion} applies. For a peripheral conjugate,
+  \(\gamma^{hn+r}=\gamma^r\rho^n\).
+  If \(\lvert\gamma\rvert<\beta\), then
+  \(\lvert\gamma^h\rvert<\rho\). If such conjugates exist, their total
+  contribution is \(O(\theta^n)\), where
+  \(\theta=\max_{\lvert\gamma\rvert<\beta}\lvert\gamma\rvert^h<\rho\);
+  if none exist, that contribution is identically zero and we choose any
+  \(0<\theta<\rho\). Therefore, for
+  every fixed residue \(r\),
+  \[
+    U_{hn+r}=C_r\rho^n+O(\theta^n)
+             =C_r\rho^n+o(\rho^n)
+    \qquad(n\ge N_r).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-residue-asymptotic}
+  \]
+  In particular,
+  \[
+    C_r=\lim_{n\to\infty}\rho^{-n}U_{hn+r}.
+  \]
+  The right-hand side is a limit of real nonnegative numbers, so
+  \(C_r\in\mathbb R\) and \(C_r\ge0\).
+
+  At least one residue coefficient is nonzero. To see this without any
+  suppressed independence argument, list the peripheral conjugates as
+  \(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_s\), and write
+  \(\gamma_j=\beta\zeta_j\). The \(\zeta_j\) are distinct \(h\)-th
+  roots of unity, so \(s\le h\). If \(C_r=0\) for every
+  \(0\le r<h\), then
+  \[
+    0=\beta^{-r}C_r
+      =\sum_{j=1}^s A_{\gamma_j}\zeta_j^r
+      \qquad(0\le r<h).
+      \label{eq:weak-perron-fourier-system}
+  \]
+  The \(h\times s\) Fourier--Vandermonde matrix
+  \[
+    (\zeta_j^r)_{\substack{0\le r<h\\1\le j\le s}}
+  \]
+  has full column rank: its first \(s\) rows form a square Vandermonde
+  matrix with determinant
+  \(\prod_{1\le i<j\le s}(\zeta_j-\zeta_i)\ne0\).
+  Equation \eqref{eq:weak-perron-fourier-system} would force all
+  peripheral coefficients to vanish,
+  including \(A_\beta\), a contradiction.
+
+  \emph{Cyclic propagation of positivity.}
+  Choose \(r\) with \(C_r>0\). If \(r<h-1\), then for all sufficiently
+  large \(n\), strict increase gives
+  \[
+    U_{hn+r}<U_{hn+r+1}.
+  \]
+  Divide by \(\rho^n\) and use
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-residue-asymptotic} for both residue classes. The
+  limiting inequality gives \(C_r\le C_{r+1}\), so in particular
+  \(C_{r+1}>0\). At the wraparound, strict increase gives
+  \[
+    U_{hn+h-1}<U_{h(n+1)},
+    \qquad
+    \rho^{-n}U_{h(n+1)}\longrightarrow\rho C_0,
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-wraparound-limit}
+  \]
+  whereas \(\rho^{-n}U_{hn+h-1}\to C_{h-1}\). Thus
+  \(C_{h-1}\le\rho C_0\), and \(C_{h-1}>0\) forces \(C_0>0\).
+  Starting from one positive coefficient and moving cyclically proves
+  \[
+    C_r>0\qquad(0\le r<h).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-positive-residues}
+  \]
+
+  Finally, if \(N=hn+r\), then
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-residue-asymptotic} and
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-positive-residues} give
+  \begin{align*}
+    U_N&=C_r\rho^n(1+o(1)),\\
+    \frac{\log U_N}{N}
+      &=\frac{n\log\rho+\log C_r+o(1)}{hn+r}
+        \longrightarrow\frac{\log\rho}{h}=\log\beta.
+  \end{align*}
+  There are only finitely many residues, so this proves the global limit
+  \[
+    \lim_{N\to\infty}U_N^{1/N}=\beta.
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-global-root-limit}
+  \]

+\paragraph{Greedy length interval.}
+For a standard greedy linear numeration basis with \(U_0=1\), a positive
+integer has a canonical greedy word of length \(m\) if and only if it lies
+in the half-open interval
+\[
+  [U_{m-1},U_m).

+Indeed, the greedy algorithm chooses the least threshold \(U_m\) strictly
+larger than the represented integer; minimality of \(m\) gives the lower
+bound, and the choice of \(U_m\) gives the upper bound. This is a property
+of the standard greedy subclass, not an assumption on the ambient
+canonical eventually recurrent systems.

+  We first establish the asymptotic needed for
+  \textup{(ii)}\(\Rightarrow\)\textup{(iii)}. This conclusion is also
+  obtainable from Charlier--Kreczman's quotient-limit mechanism
+  \cite[Proposition~10 and Remark~12]{CharlierKreczman2025}; we give the
+  coefficient-level argument because the residue thresholds and positivity
+  are part of the hypotheses used here.
+
+  \emph{Peripheral period.}
+  The classical power characterization of weak Perron numbers gives an
+  integer \(h\ge1\) for which
+  \[
+    \rho:=\beta^h
+  \]
+  is a Perron number \cite{Brunotte2013,Lind1984}. Equivalently, if
+  \(\gamma\) is any conjugate of \(\beta\), then
+  \[
+    \lvert\gamma\rvert=\beta\ \Longrightarrow\ \gamma^h=\rho,
+    \qquad
+    \lvert\gamma\rvert<\beta\ \Longrightarrow\
+      \lvert\gamma^h\rvert<\rho.
+  \]
+  In particular, every peripheral phase \(\gamma/\beta\) is an
+  \(h\)-th root of unity; the conclusion is stronger than merely placing
+  \(\gamma^h\) somewhere on the circle of radius \(\rho\).
+
+  \emph{Tail coefficients and their covariance.}
+  Put \(d=\deg\mu_U\), let \(K\) be a splitting field of \(\mu_U\), and
+  let \(J_{\mathrm r}\) be the threshold from which \(\mu_U\) annihilates
+  \(U\). The irreducible polynomial \(\mu_U\in\mathbb Q[X]\) is
+  separable. Hence there are unique coefficients \(A_\gamma\in K\), one
+  for each conjugate \(\gamma\) of \(\beta\), such that
+  \[
+    U_n=\sum_\gamma A_\gamma\gamma^n
+    \qquad(n\ge J_{\mathrm r}).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-tail-expansion}
+  \]
+  Indeed, the coefficients are determined by the \(d\) values with
+  \(n=J_{\mathrm r},\ldots,J_{\mathrm r}+d-1\); the corresponding matrix
+  is a nonsingular Vandermonde matrix multiplied by the nonzero diagonal
+  matrix \(\operatorname{diag}(\gamma^{J_{\mathrm r}})\). No polynomial
+  factors in \(n\) occur because every root is simple.
+
+  For \(\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(K/\mathbb Q)\), applying \(\sigma\)
+  to \eqref{eq:weak-perron-tail-expansion} and using
+  \(U_n\in\mathbb Q\) gives
+  \[
+    U_n=\sum_\gamma \sigma(A_\gamma)\sigma(\gamma)^n.
+  \]
+  Uniqueness of the expansion therefore yields the explicit covariance
+  identity
+  \[
+    A_{\sigma(\gamma)}=\sigma(A_\gamma).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-galois-covariance}
+  \]
+  For each conjugate \(\gamma\), the embedding
+  \(\mathbb Q(\beta)\hookrightarrow K\) that sends \(\beta\) to
+  \(\gamma\) extends to an automorphism of the splitting field \(K\).
+  Thus, if \(A_\beta=0\),
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-galois-covariance} forces every \(A_\gamma\) to vanish,
+  contradicting the positive, nonzero tail of \(U\). Consequently
+  \(A_\beta\ne0\); the same argument in fact shows that every
+  \(A_\gamma\ne0\).
+
+  \emph{Residue asymptotics.}
+  For each \(r\in\{0,\ldots,h-1\}\), set
+  \[
+    N_r:=\max\!\left\{0,
+      \left\lceil\frac{J_{\mathrm r}-r}{h}\right\rceil\right\},
+    \qquad
+    C_r:=\sum_{\lvert\gamma\rvert=\beta}A_\gamma\gamma^r.
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-residue-threshold-coefficient}
+  \]
+  Then \(hn+r\ge J_{\mathrm r}\) whenever \(n\ge N_r\), so
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-tail-expansion} applies. For a peripheral conjugate,
+  \(\gamma^{hn+r}=\gamma^r\rho^n\).
+  If \(\lvert\gamma\rvert<\beta\), then
+  \(\lvert\gamma^h\rvert<\rho\). If such conjugates exist, their total
+  contribution is \(O(\theta^n)\), where
+  \(\theta=\max_{\lvert\gamma\rvert<\beta}\lvert\gamma\rvert^h<\rho\);
+  if none exist, that contribution is identically zero and we choose any
+  \(0<\theta<\rho\). Therefore, for
+  every fixed residue \(r\),
+  \[
+    U_{hn+r}=C_r\rho^n+O(\theta^n)
+             =C_r\rho^n+o(\rho^n)
+    \qquad(n\ge N_r).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-residue-asymptotic}
+  \]
+  In particular,
+  \[
+    C_r=\lim_{n\to\infty}\rho^{-n}U_{hn+r}.
+  \]
+  The right-hand side is a limit of real nonnegative numbers, so
+  \(C_r\in\mathbb R\) and \(C_r\ge0\).
+
+  At least one residue coefficient is nonzero. To see this without any
+  suppressed independence argument, list the peripheral conjugates as
+  \(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_s\), and write
+  \(\gamma_j=\beta\zeta_j\). The \(\zeta_j\) are distinct \(h\)-th
+  roots of unity, so \(s\le h\). If \(C_r=0\) for every
+  \(0\le r<h\), then
+  \[
+    0=\beta^{-r}C_r
+      =\sum_{j=1}^s A_{\gamma_j}\zeta_j^r
+      \qquad(0\le r<h).
+      \label{eq:weak-perron-fourier-system}
+  \]
+  The \(h\times s\) Fourier--Vandermonde matrix
+  \[
+    (\zeta_j^r)_{\substack{0\le r<h\\1\le j\le s}}
+  \]
+  has full column rank: its first \(s\) rows form a square Vandermonde
+  matrix with determinant
+  \(\prod_{1\le i<j\le s}(\zeta_j-\zeta_i)\ne0\).
+  Equation \eqref{eq:weak-perron-fourier-system} would force all
+  peripheral coefficients to vanish,
+  including \(A_\beta\), a contradiction.
+
+  \emph{Cyclic propagation of positivity.}
+  Choose \(r\) with \(C_r>0\). If \(r<h-1\), then for all sufficiently
+  large \(n\), strict increase gives
+  \[
+    U_{hn+r}<U_{hn+r+1}.
+  \]
+  Divide by \(\rho^n\) and use
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-residue-asymptotic} for both residue classes. The
+  limiting inequality gives \(C_r\le C_{r+1}\), so in particular
+  \(C_{r+1}>0\). At the wraparound, strict increase gives
+  \[
+    U_{hn+h-1}<U_{h(n+1)},
+    \qquad
+    \rho^{-n}U_{h(n+1)}\longrightarrow\rho C_0,
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-wraparound-limit}
+  \]
+  whereas \(\rho^{-n}U_{hn+h-1}\to C_{h-1}\). Thus
+  \(C_{h-1}\le\rho C_0\), and \(C_{h-1}>0\) forces \(C_0>0\).
+  Starting from one positive coefficient and moving cyclically proves
+  \[
+    C_r>0\qquad(0\le r<h).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-positive-residues}
+  \]
+
+  Finally, if \(N=hn+r\), then
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-residue-asymptotic} and
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-positive-residues} give
+  \begin{align*}
+    U_N&=C_r\rho^n(1+o(1)),\\
+    \frac{\log U_N}{N}
+      &=\frac{n\log\rho+\log C_r+o(1)}{hn+r}
+        \longrightarrow\frac{\log\rho}{h}=\log\beta.
+  \end{align*}
+  There are only finitely many residues, so this proves the global limit
+  \[
+    \lim_{N\to\infty}U_N^{1/N}=\beta.
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-global-root-limit}
+  \]

+eventually increasing. Under the irreducible weak-Perron hypotheses below,
+separability gives equal peripheral multiplicities, weak-Perron periodicity
+gives the common power, and strict increase supplies their last hypothesis.
+Thus their work already contains the root-growth mechanism needed for our
+length squeeze, in essentially equivalent quotient-limit form. We retain a
+self-contained coefficient-level proof because it identifies every residue
+coefficient and verifies positivity under exactly our hypotheses. Their
+regularity characterization neither assumes nor concludes anything about
+MCFL sublanguages, bounded prime support, synchronized geometric schemes, or
+the five equivalent conditions proved here; conversely, our theorem does not
+characterize regularity of the whole greedy language.

+\paragraph{Greedy length interval.}
+For a standard greedy linear numeration basis with \(U_0=1\), a positive
+integer has a canonical greedy word of length \(m\) if and only if it lies
+in the half-open interval
+\[
+  [U_{m-1},U_m).
+\]
+Indeed, the greedy algorithm chooses the least threshold \(U_m\) strictly
+larger than the represented integer; minimality of \(m\) gives the lower
+bound, and the choice of \(U_m\) gives the upper bound. This is a property
+of the standard greedy subclass, not an assumption on the ambient
+canonical eventually recurrent systems.
+

+  We first establish the asymptotic needed for
+  \textup{(ii)}\(\Rightarrow\)\textup{(iii)}. This conclusion is also
+  obtainable from Charlier--Kreczman's quotient-limit mechanism
+  \cite[Proposition~10 and Remark~12]{CharlierKreczman2025}; we give the
+  coefficient-level argument because the residue thresholds and positivity
+  are part of the hypotheses used here.
+
+  \emph{Peripheral period.}
+  The classical power characterization of weak Perron numbers gives an
+  integer \(h\ge1\) for which
+  \[
+    \rho:=\beta^h
+  \]
+  is a Perron number \cite{Brunotte2013,Lind1984}. Equivalently, if
+  \(\gamma\) is any conjugate of \(\beta\), then
+  \[
+    \lvert\gamma\rvert=\beta\ \Longrightarrow\ \gamma^h=\rho,
+    \qquad
+    \lvert\gamma\rvert<\beta\ \Longrightarrow\
+      \lvert\gamma^h\rvert<\rho.
+  \]
+  In particular, every peripheral phase \(\gamma/\beta\) is an
+  \(h\)-th root of unity; the conclusion is stronger than merely placing
+  \(\gamma^h\) somewhere on the circle of radius \(\rho\).
+
+  \emph{Tail coefficients and their covariance.}
+  Put \(d=\deg\mu_U\), let \(K\) be a splitting field of \(\mu_U\), and
+  let \(J_{\mathrm r}\) be the threshold from which \(\mu_U\) annihilates
+  \(U\). The irreducible polynomial \(\mu_U\in\mathbb Q[X]\) is
+  separable. Hence there are unique coefficients \(A_\gamma\in K\), one
+  for each conjugate \(\gamma\) of \(\beta\), such that
+  \[
+    U_n=\sum_\gamma A_\gamma\gamma^n
+    \qquad(n\ge J_{\mathrm r}).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-tail-expansion}
+  \]
+  Indeed, the coefficients are determined by the \(d\) values with
+  \(n=J_{\mathrm r},\ldots,J_{\mathrm r}+d-1\); the corresponding matrix
+  is a nonsingular Vandermonde matrix multiplied by the nonzero diagonal
+  matrix \(\operatorname{diag}(\gamma^{J_{\mathrm r}})\). No polynomial
+  factors in \(n\) occur because every root is simple.
+
+  For \(\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(K/\mathbb Q)\), applying \(\sigma\)
+  to \eqref{eq:weak-perron-tail-expansion} and using
+  \(U_n\in\mathbb Q\) gives
+  \[
+    U_n=\sum_\gamma \sigma(A_\gamma)\sigma(\gamma)^n.
+  \]
+  Uniqueness of the expansion therefore yields the explicit covariance
+  identity
+  \[
+    A_{\sigma(\gamma)}=\sigma(A_\gamma).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-galois-covariance}
+  \]
+  For each conjugate \(\gamma\), the embedding
+  \(\mathbb Q(\beta)\hookrightarrow K\) that sends \(\beta\) to
+  \(\gamma\) extends to an automorphism of the splitting field \(K\).
+  Thus, if \(A_\beta=0\),
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-galois-covariance} forces every \(A_\gamma\) to vanish,
+  contradicting the positive, nonzero tail of \(U\). Consequently
+  \(A_\beta\ne0\); the same argument in fact shows that every
+  \(A_\gamma\ne0\).
+
+  \emph{Residue asymptotics.}
+  For each \(r\in\{0,\ldots,h-1\}\), set
+  \[
+    N_r:=\max\!\left\{0,
+      \left\lceil\frac{J_{\mathrm r}-r}{h}\right\rceil\right\},
+    \qquad
+    C_r:=\sum_{\lvert\gamma\rvert=\beta}A_\gamma\gamma^r.
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-residue-threshold-coefficient}
+  \]
+  Then \(hn+r\ge J_{\mathrm r}\) whenever \(n\ge N_r\), so
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-tail-expansion} applies. For a peripheral conjugate,
+  \(\gamma^{hn+r}=\gamma^r\rho^n\).
+  If \(\lvert\gamma\rvert<\beta\), then
+  \(\lvert\gamma^h\rvert<\rho\). If such conjugates exist, their total
+  contribution is \(O(\theta^n)\), where
+  \(\theta=\max_{\lvert\gamma\rvert<\beta}\lvert\gamma\rvert^h<\rho\);
+  if none exist, that contribution is identically zero and we choose any
+  \(0<\theta<\rho\). Therefore, for
+  every fixed residue \(r\),
+  \[
+    U_{hn+r}=C_r\rho^n+O(\theta^n)
+             =C_r\rho^n+o(\rho^n)
+    \qquad(n\ge N_r).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-residue-asymptotic}
+  \]
+  In particular,
+  \[
+    C_r=\lim_{n\to\infty}\rho^{-n}U_{hn+r}.
+  \]
+  The right-hand side is a limit of real nonnegative numbers, so
+  \(C_r\in\mathbb R\) and \(C_r\ge0\).
+
+  At least one residue coefficient is nonzero. To see this without any
+  suppressed independence argument, list the peripheral conjugates as
+  \(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_s\), and write
+  \(\gamma_j=\beta\zeta_j\). The \(\zeta_j\) are distinct \(h\)-th
+  roots of unity, so \(s\le h\). If \(C_r=0\) for every
+  \(0\le r<h\), then
+  \[
+    0=\beta^{-r}C_r
+      =\sum_{j=1}^s A_{\gamma_j}\zeta_j^r
+      \qquad(0\le r<h).
+      \label{eq:weak-perron-fourier-system}
+  \]
+  The \(h\times s\) Fourier--Vandermonde matrix
+  \[
+    (\zeta_j^r)_{\substack{0\le r<h\\1\le j\le s}}
+  \]
+  has full column rank: its first \(s\) rows form a square Vandermonde
+  matrix with determinant
+  \(\prod_{1\le i<j\le s}(\zeta_j-\zeta_i)\ne0\).
+  Equation \eqref{eq:weak-perron-fourier-system} would force all
+  peripheral coefficients to vanish,
+  including \(A_\beta\), a contradiction.
+
+  \emph{Cyclic propagation of positivity.}
+  Choose \(r\) with \(C_r>0\). If \(r<h-1\), then for all sufficiently
+  large \(n\), strict increase gives
+  \[
+    U_{hn+r}<U_{hn+r+1}.
+  \]
+  Divide by \(\rho^n\) and use
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-residue-asymptotic} for both residue classes. The
+  limiting inequality gives \(C_r\le C_{r+1}\), so in particular
+  \(C_{r+1}>0\). At the wraparound, strict increase gives
+  \[
+    U_{hn+h-1}<U_{h(n+1)},
+    \qquad
+    \rho^{-n}U_{h(n+1)}\longrightarrow\rho C_0,
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-wraparound-limit}
+  \]
+  whereas \(\rho^{-n}U_{hn+h-1}\to C_{h-1}\). Thus
+  \(C_{h-1}\le\rho C_0\), and \(C_{h-1}>0\) forces \(C_0>0\).
+  Starting from one positive coefficient and moving cyclically proves
+  \[
+    C_r>0\qquad(0\le r<h).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-positive-residues}
+  \]
+
+  Finally, if \(N=hn+r\), then
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-residue-asymptotic} and
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-positive-residues} give
+  \begin{align*}
+    U_N&=C_r\rho^n(1+o(1)),\\
+    \frac{\log U_N}{N}
+      &=\frac{n\log\rho+\log C_r+o(1)}{hn+r}
+        \longrightarrow\frac{\log\rho}{h}=\log\beta.
+  \end{align*}
+  There are only finitely many residues, so this proves the global limit
+  \[
+    \lim_{N\to\infty}U_N^{1/N}=\beta.
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-global-root-limit}
+  \]

 108:   The \(h\times s\) Fourier--Vandermonde matrix
 109:   \[
 110:     (\zeta_j^r)_{\substack{0\le r<h\\1\le j\le s}}
 111:   \]
 112:   has full column rank: its first \(s\) rows form a square Vandermonde
 113:   matrix with determinant
 114:   \(\prod_{1\le i<j\le s}(\zeta_j-\zeta_i)\ne0\).
 115:   Equation \eqref{eq:weak-perron-fourier-system} would force all
 116:   peripheral coefficients to vanish,
 117:   including \(A_\beta\), a contradiction.
 118: 
 119:   \emph{Cyclic propagation of positivity.}
 120:   Choose \(r\) with \(C_r>0\). If \(r<h-1\), then for all sufficiently
 121:   large \(n\), strict increase gives
 122:   \[
 123:     U_{hn+r}<U_{hn+r+1}.
 124:   \]
 125:   Divide by \(\rho^n\) and use
 126:   \eqref{eq:weak-perron-residue-asymptotic} for both residue classes. The
 127:   limiting inequality gives \(C_r\le C_{r+1}\), so in particular
 128:   \(C_{r+1}>0\). At the wraparound, strict increase gives
 129:   \[
 130:     U_{hn+h-1}<U_{h(n+1)},
 131:     \qquad
 132:     \rho^{-n}U_{h(n+1)}\longrightarrow\rho C_0,
 133:     \label{eq:weak-perron-wraparound-limit}
 134:   \]
 135:   whereas \(\rho^{-n}U_{hn+h-1}\to C_{h-1}\). Thus
 136:   \(C_{h-1}\le\rho C_0\), and \(C_{h-1}>0\) forces \(C_0>0\).
 137:   Starting from one positive coefficient and moving cyclically proves
 138:   \[
 139:     C_r>0\qquad(0\le r<h).
 140:     \label{eq:weak-perron-positive-residues}
 141:   \]
 142: 
 143:   Finally, if \(N=hn+r\), then
 144:   \eqref{eq:weak-perron-residue-asymptotic} and
 145:   \eqref{eq:weak-perron-positive-residues} give
 146:   \begin{align*}
 147:     U_N&=C_r\rho^n(1+o(1)),\\
 148:     \frac{\log U_N}{N}
 149:       &=\frac{n\log\rho+\log C_r+o(1)}{hn+r}
 150:         \longrightarrow\frac{\log\rho}{h}=\log\beta.
 151:   \end{align*}
 152:   There are only finitely many residues, so this proves the global limit
 153:   \[
 154:     \lim_{N\to\infty}U_N^{1/N}=\beta.
 155:     \label{eq:weak-perron-global-root-limit}
 156:   \]

+\paragraph{Greedy length interval.}
+For a standard greedy linear numeration basis with \(U_0=1\), a positive

+  We first establish the asymptotic needed for
+  \textup{(ii)}\(\Rightarrow\)\textup{(iii)}. This conclusion is also
+  obtainable from Charlier--Kreczman's quotient-limit mechanism
+  \cite[Proposition~10 and Remark~12]{CharlierKreczman2025}; we give the
+  coefficient-level argument because the residue thresholds and positivity
+  are part of the hypotheses used here.
+
+  \emph{Peripheral period.}
+  The classical power characterization of weak Perron numbers gives an
+  integer \(h\ge1\) for which
+  \[
+    \rho:=\beta^h
+  \]
+  is a Perron number \cite{Brunotte2013,Lind1984}. Equivalently, if
+  \(\gamma\) is any conjugate of \(\beta\), then
+  \[
+    \lvert\gamma\rvert=\beta\ \Longrightarrow\ \gamma^h=\rho,
+    \qquad
+    \lvert\gamma\rvert<\beta\ \Longrightarrow\
+      \lvert\gamma^h\rvert<\rho.
+  \]
+  In particular, every peripheral phase \(\gamma/\beta\) is an
+  \(h\)-th root of unity; the conclusion is stronger than merely placing
+  \(\gamma^h\) somewhere on the circle of radius \(\rho\).
+
+  \emph{Tail coefficients and their covariance.}
+  Put \(d=\deg\mu_U\), let \(K\) be a splitting field of \(\mu_U\), and
+  let \(J_{\mathrm r}\) be the threshold from which \(\mu_U\) annihilates
+  \(U\). The irreducible polynomial \(\mu_U\in\mathbb Q[X]\) is
+  separable. Hence there are unique coefficients \(A_\gamma\in K\), one
+  for each conjugate \(\gamma\) of \(\beta\), such that
+  \[
+    U_n=\sum_\gamma A_\gamma\gamma^n
+    \qquad(n\ge J_{\mathrm r}).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-tail-expansion}
+  \]
+  Indeed, the coefficients are determined by the \(d\) values with
+  \(n=J_{\mathrm r},\ldots,J_{\mathrm r}+d-1\); the corresponding matrix
+  is a nonsingular Vandermonde matrix multiplied by the nonzero diagonal
+  matrix \(\operatorname{diag}(\gamma^{J_{\mathrm r}})\). No polynomial
+  factors in \(n\) occur because every root is simple.
+
+  For \(\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(K/\mathbb Q)\), applying \(\sigma\)
+  to \eqref{eq:weak-perron-tail-expansion} and using
+  \(U_n\in\mathbb Q\) gives
+  \[
+    U_n=\sum_\gamma \sigma(A_\gamma)\sigma(\gamma)^n.
+  \]
+  Uniqueness of the expansion therefore yields the explicit covariance
+  identity
+  \[
+    A_{\sigma(\gamma)}=\sigma(A_\gamma).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-galois-covariance}
+  \]
+  For each conjugate \(\gamma\), the embedding
+  \(\mathbb Q(\beta)\hookrightarrow K\) that sends \(\beta\) to
+  \(\gamma\) extends to an automorphism of the splitting field \(K\).
+  Thus, if \(A_\beta=0\),
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-galois-covariance} forces every \(A_\gamma\) to vanish,
+  contradicting the positive, nonzero tail of \(U\). Consequently
+  \(A_\beta\ne0\); the same argument in fact shows that every
+  \(A_\gamma\ne0\).
+
+  \emph{Residue asymptotics.}
+  For each \(r\in\{0,\ldots,h-1\}\), set
+  \[
+    N_r:=\max\!\left\{0,
+      \left\lceil\frac{J_{\mathrm r}-r}{h}\right\rceil\right\},
+    \qquad
+    C_r:=\sum_{\lvert\gamma\rvert=\beta}A_\gamma\gamma^r.
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-residue-threshold-coefficient}
+  \]
+  Then \(hn+r\ge J_{\mathrm r}\) whenever \(n\ge N_r\), so
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-tail-expansion} applies. For a peripheral conjugate,
+  \(\gamma^{hn+r}=\gamma^r\rho^n\).
+  If \(\lvert\gamma\rvert<\beta\), then
+  \(\lvert\gamma^h\rvert<\rho\). If such conjugates exist, their total
+  contribution is \(O(\theta^n)\), where
+  \(\theta=\max_{\lvert\gamma\rvert<\beta}\lvert\gamma\rvert^h<\rho\);
+  if none exist, that contribution is identically zero and we choose any
+  \(0<\theta<\rho\). Therefore, for
+  every fixed residue \(r\),
+  \[
+    U_{hn+r}=C_r\rho^n+O(\theta^n)
+             =C_r\rho^n+o(\rho^n)
+    \qquad(n\ge N_r).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-residue-asymptotic}
+  \]
+  In particular,
+  \[
+    C_r=\lim_{n\to\infty}\rho^{-n}U_{hn+r}.
+  \]
+  The right-hand side is a limit of real nonnegative numbers, so
+  \(C_r\in\mathbb R\) and \(C_r\ge0\).
+
+  At least one residue coefficient is nonzero. To see this without any
+  suppressed independence argument, list the peripheral conjugates as
+  \(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_s\), and write
+  \(\gamma_j=\beta\zeta_j\). The \(\zeta_j\) are distinct \(h\)-th
+  roots of unity, so \(s\le h\). If \(C_r=0\) for every
+  \(0\le r<h\), then
+  \[
+    0=\beta^{-r}C_r
+      =\sum_{j=1}^s A_{\gamma_j}\zeta_j^r
+      \qquad(0\le r<h).
+      \label{eq:weak-perron-fourier-system}
+  \]
+  The \(h\times s\) Fourier--Vandermonde matrix
+  \[
+    (\zeta_j^r)_{\substack{0\le r<h\\1\le j\le s}}
+  \]
+  has full column rank: its first \(s\) rows form a square Vandermonde
+  matrix with determinant
+  \(\prod_{1\le i<j\le s}(\zeta_j-\zeta_i)\ne0\).
+  Equation \eqref{eq:weak-perron-fourier-system} would force all
+  peripheral coefficients to vanish,
+  including \(A_\beta\), a contradiction.
+
+  \emph{Cyclic propagation of positivity.}
+  Choose \(r\) with \(C_r>0\). If \(r<h-1\), then for all sufficiently
+  large \(n\), strict increase gives
+  \[
+    U_{hn+r}<U_{hn+r+1}.
+  \]
+  Divide by \(\rho^n\) and use
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-residue-asymptotic} for both residue classes. The
+  limiting inequality gives \(C_r\le C_{r+1}\), so in particular
+  \(C_{r+1}>0\). At the wraparound, strict increase gives
+  \[
+    U_{hn+h-1}<U_{h(n+1)},
+    \qquad
+    \rho^{-n}U_{h(n+1)}\longrightarrow\rho C_0,
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-wraparound-limit}
+  \]
+  whereas \(\rho^{-n}U_{hn+h-1}\to C_{h-1}\). Thus
+  \(C_{h-1}\le\rho C_0\), and \(C_{h-1}>0\) forces \(C_0>0\).
+  Starting from one positive coefficient and moving cyclically proves
+  \[
+    C_r>0\qquad(0\le r<h).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-positive-residues}
+  \]
+
+  Finally, if \(N=hn+r\), then
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-residue-asymptotic} and
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-positive-residues} give
+  \begin{align*}
+    U_N&=C_r\rho^n(1+o(1)),\\
+    \frac{\log U_N}{N}
+      &=\frac{n\log\rho+\log C_r+o(1)}{hn+r}
+        \longrightarrow\frac{\log\rho}{h}=\log\beta.
+  \end{align*}
+  There are only finitely many residues, so this proves the global limit
+  \[
+    \lim_{N\to\infty}U_N^{1/N}=\beta.
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-global-root-limit}
+  \]

+\paragraph{Greedy length interval.}
+For a standard greedy linear numeration basis with \(U_0=1\), a positive
+integer has a canonical greedy word of length \(m\) if and only if it lies
+in the half-open interval
+\[

+canonical eventually recurrent systems.

+  We first establish the asymptotic needed for

+  \emph{Peripheral period.}
+  The classical power characterization of weak Perron numbers gives an
+  integer \(h\ge1\) for which
+  \[

+  \]
+  is a Perron number \cite{Brunotte2013,Lind1984}. Equivalently, if
+  \(\gamma\) is any conjugate of \(\beta\), then

+  \]
+  In particular, every peripheral phase \(\gamma/\beta\) is an
+  \(h\)-th root of unity; the conclusion is stronger than merely placing
+  \(\gamma^h\) somewhere on the circle of radius \(\rho\).

+  \emph{Tail coefficients and their covariance.}
+  Put \(d=\deg\mu_U\), let \(K\) be a splitting field of \(\mu_U\), and
+  let \(J_{\mathrm r}\) be the threshold from which \(\mu_U\) annihilates
+  \(U\). The irreducible polynomial \(\mu_U\in\mathbb Q[X]\) is
+  separable. Hence there are unique coefficients \(A_\gamma\in K\), one
+  for each conjugate \(\gamma\) of \(\beta\), such that
+  \begin{equation}
+    U_n=\sum_\gamma A_\gamma\gamma^n
+    \qquad(n\ge J_{\mathrm r}).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-tail-expansion}
+  \end{equation}
+  Indeed, the coefficients are determined by the \(d\) values with
+  \(n=J_{\mathrm r},\ldots,J_{\mathrm r}+d-1\); the corresponding matrix
+  is a nonsingular Vandermonde matrix multiplied by the nonzero diagonal
+  matrix \(\operatorname{diag}(\gamma^{J_{\mathrm r}})\). No polynomial
+  factors in \(n\) occur because every root is simple.
+
+  For \(\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(K/\mathbb Q)\), applying \(\sigma\)
+  to \eqref{eq:weak-perron-tail-expansion} and using
+  \(U_n\in\mathbb Q\) gives
+  \[
+    U_n=\sum_\gamma \sigma(A_\gamma)\sigma(\gamma)^n.
+  \]
+  Uniqueness of the expansion therefore yields the explicit covariance
+  identity
+  \begin{equation}
+    A_{\sigma(\gamma)}=\sigma(A_\gamma).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-galois-covariance}
+  \end{equation}
+  For each conjugate \(\gamma\), the embedding
+  \(\mathbb Q(\beta)\hookrightarrow K\) that sends \(\beta\) to
+  \(\gamma\) extends to an automorphism of the splitting field \(K\).
+  Thus, if \(A_\beta=0\),
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-galois-covariance} forces every \(A_\gamma\) to vanish,
+  contradicting the positive, nonzero tail of \(U\). Consequently
+  \(A_\beta\ne0\); the same argument in fact shows that every
+  \(A_\gamma\ne0\).
+
+  \emph{Residue asymptotics.}
+  For each \(r\in\{0,\ldots,h-1\}\), set
+  \begin{equation}
+    N_r:=\max\!\left\{0,
+      \left\lceil\frac{J_{\mathrm r}-r}{h}\right\rceil\right\},
+    \qquad
+    C_r:=\sum_{\lvert\gamma\rvert=\beta}A_\gamma\gamma^r.
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-residue-threshold-coefficient}
+  \end{equation}
+  Then \(hn+r\ge J_{\mathrm r}\) whenever \(n\ge N_r\), so
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-tail-expansion} applies. For a peripheral conjugate,
+  \(\gamma^{hn+r}=\gamma^r\rho^n\).
+  If \(\lvert\gamma\rvert<\beta\), then
+  \(\lvert\gamma^h\rvert<\rho\). If such conjugates exist, their total
+  contribution is \(O(\theta^n)\), where
+  \(\theta=\max_{\lvert\gamma\rvert<\beta}\lvert\gamma\rvert^h<\rho\);
+  if none exist, that contribution is identically zero and we choose any
+  \(0<\theta<\rho\). Therefore, for
+  every fixed residue \(r\),
+  \begin{equation}
+    U_{hn+r}=C_r\rho^n+O(\theta^n)
+             =C_r\rho^n+o(\rho^n)
+    \qquad(n\ge N_r).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-residue-asymptotic}
+  \end{equation}
+  In particular,
+  \[
+    C_r=\lim_{n\to\infty}\rho^{-n}U_{hn+r}.
+  \]
+  The right-hand side is a limit of real nonnegative numbers, so
+  \(C_r\in\mathbb R\) and \(C_r\ge0\).
+
+  At least one residue coefficient is nonzero. To see this without any
+  suppressed independence argument, list the peripheral conjugates as
+  \(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_s\), and write
+  \(\gamma_j=\beta\zeta_j\). The \(\zeta_j\) are distinct \(h\)-th
+  roots of unity, so \(s\le h\). If \(C_r=0\) for every
+  \(0\le r<h\), then
+  \begin{equation}
+    0=\beta^{-r}C_r
+      =\sum_{j=1}^s A_{\gamma_j}\zeta_j^r
+      \qquad(0\le r<h).
+      \label{eq:weak-perron-fourier-system}
+  \end{equation}
+  The \(h\times s\) Fourier--Vandermonde matrix
+  \[
+    (\zeta_j^r)_{\substack{0\le r<h\\1\le j\le s}}
+  \]
+  has full column rank: its first \(s\) rows form a square Vandermonde
+  matrix with determinant
+  \(\prod_{1\le i<j\le s}(\zeta_j-\zeta_i)\ne0\).
+  Equation \eqref{eq:weak-perron-fourier-system} would force all
+  peripheral coefficients to vanish,
+  including \(A_\beta\), a contradiction.
+
+  \emph{Cyclic propagation of positivity.}
+  Choose \(r\) with \(C_r>0\). If \(r<h-1\), then for all sufficiently
+  large \(n\), strict increase gives
+  \[
+    U_{hn+r}<U_{hn+r+1}.
+  \]
+  Divide by \(\rho^n\) and use
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-residue-asymptotic} for both residue classes. The
+  limiting inequality gives \(C_r\le C_{r+1}\), so in particular
+  \(C_{r+1}>0\). At the wraparound, strict increase gives
+  \begin{equation}
+    U_{hn+h-1}<U_{h(n+1)},
+    \qquad
+    \rho^{-n}U_{h(n+1)}\longrightarrow\rho C_0,
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-wraparound-limit}
+  \end{equation}
+  whereas \(\rho^{-n}U_{hn+h-1}\to C_{h-1}\). Thus
+  \(C_{h-1}\le\rho C_0\), and \(C_{h-1}>0\) forces \(C_0>0\).
+  Starting from one positive coefficient and moving cyclically proves
+  \begin{equation}
+    C_r>0\qquad(0\le r<h).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-positive-residues}
+  \end{equation}
+
+  Finally, if \(N=hn+r\), then
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-residue-asymptotic} and
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-positive-residues} give
+  \begin{align*}
+    U_N&=C_r\rho^n(1+o(1)),\\
+    \frac{\log U_N}{N}
+      &=\frac{n\log\rho+\log C_r+o(1)}{hn+r}
+        \longrightarrow\frac{\log\rho}{h}=\log\beta.
+  \end{align*}
+  There are only finitely many residues, so this proves the global limit
+  \begin{equation}
+    \lim_{N\to\infty}U_N^{1/N}=\beta.
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-global-root-limit}
+  \end{equation}

+  We first establish the asymptotic needed for
+  \textup{(ii)}\(\Rightarrow\)\textup{(iii)}. This conclusion is also
+  obtainable from Charlier--Kreczman's quotient-limit mechanism
+  \cite[Proposition~10 and Remark~12]{CharlierKreczman2025}; we give the
+  coefficient-level argument because the residue thresholds and positivity
+  are part of the hypotheses used here.
+
+  \emph{Peripheral period.}
+  The classical power characterization of weak Perron numbers gives an
+  integer \(h\ge1\) for which
+  \[
+    \rho:=\beta^h
+  \]
+  is a Perron number \cite{Brunotte2013,Lind1984}. Equivalently, if
+  \(\gamma\) is any conjugate of \(\beta\), then
+  \[
+    \lvert\gamma\rvert=\beta\ \Longrightarrow\ \gamma^h=\rho,
+    \qquad
+    \lvert\gamma\rvert<\beta\ \Longrightarrow\
+      \lvert\gamma^h\rvert<\rho.
+  \]
+  In particular, every peripheral phase \(\gamma/\beta\) is an
+  \(h\)-th root of unity; the conclusion is stronger than merely placing
+  \(\gamma^h\) somewhere on the circle of radius \(\rho\).
+
+  \emph{Tail coefficients and their covariance.}
+  Put \(d=\deg\mu_U\), let \(K\) be a splitting field of \(\mu_U\), and
+  let \(J_{\mathrm r}\) be the threshold from which \(\mu_U\) annihilates
+  \(U\). The irreducible polynomial \(\mu_U\in\mathbb Q[X]\) is
+  separable. Hence there are unique coefficients \(A_\gamma\in K\), one
+  for each conjugate \(\gamma\) of \(\beta\), such that
+  \begin{equation}
+    U_n=\sum_\gamma A_\gamma\gamma^n
+    \qquad(n\ge J_{\mathrm r}).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-tail-expansion}
+  \end{equation}
+  Indeed, the coefficients are determined by the \(d\) values with
+  \(n=J_{\mathrm r},\ldots,J_{\mathrm r}+d-1\); the corresponding matrix
+  is a nonsingular Vandermonde matrix multiplied by the nonzero diagonal
+  matrix \(\operatorname{diag}(\gamma^{J_{\mathrm r}})\). No polynomial
+  factors in \(n\) occur because every root is simple.
+
+  For \(\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(K/\mathbb Q)\), applying \(\sigma\)
+  to \eqref{eq:weak-perron-tail-expansion} and using
+  \(U_n\in\mathbb Q\) gives
+  \[
+    U_n=\sum_\gamma \sigma(A_\gamma)\sigma(\gamma)^n.
+  \]
+  Uniqueness of the expansion therefore yields the explicit covariance
+  identity
+  \begin{equation}
+    A_{\sigma(\gamma)}=\sigma(A_\gamma).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-galois-covariance}
+  \end{equation}
+  For each conjugate \(\gamma\), the embedding
+  \(\mathbb Q(\beta)\hookrightarrow K\) that sends \(\beta\) to
+  \(\gamma\) extends to an automorphism of the splitting field \(K\).
+  Thus, if \(A_\beta=0\),
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-galois-covariance} forces every \(A_\gamma\) to vanish,
+  contradicting the positive, nonzero tail of \(U\). Consequently
+  \(A_\beta\ne0\); the same argument in fact shows that every
+  \(A_\gamma\ne0\).
+
+  \emph{Residue asymptotics.}
+  For each \(r\in\{0,\ldots,h-1\}\), set
+  \begin{equation}
+    N_r:=\max\!\left\{0,
+      \left\lceil\frac{J_{\mathrm r}-r}{h}\right\rceil\right\},
+    \qquad
+    C_r:=\sum_{\lvert\gamma\rvert=\beta}A_\gamma\gamma^r.
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-residue-threshold-coefficient}
+  \end{equation}
+  Then \(hn+r\ge J_{\mathrm r}\) whenever \(n\ge N_r\), so
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-tail-expansion} applies. For a peripheral conjugate,
+  \(\gamma^{hn+r}=\gamma^r\rho^n\).
+  If \(\lvert\gamma\rvert<\beta\), then
+  \(\lvert\gamma^h\rvert<\rho\). If such conjugates exist, their total
+  contribution is \(O(\theta^n)\), where
+  \(\theta=\max_{\lvert\gamma\rvert<\beta}\lvert\gamma\rvert^h<\rho\);
+  if none exist, that contribution is identically zero and we choose any
+  \(0<\theta<\rho\). Therefore, for
+  every fixed residue \(r\),
+  \begin{equation}
+    U_{hn+r}=C_r\rho^n+O(\theta^n)
+             =C_r\rho^n+o(\rho^n)
+    \qquad(n\ge N_r).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-residue-asymptotic}
+  \end{equation}
+  In particular,
+  \[
+    C_r=\lim_{n\to\infty}\rho^{-n}U_{hn+r}.
+  \]
+  The right-hand side is a limit of real nonnegative numbers, so
+  \(C_r\in\mathbb R\) and \(C_r\ge0\).
+
+  At least one residue coefficient is nonzero. To see this without any
+  suppressed independence argument, list the peripheral conjugates as
+  \(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_s\), and write
+  \(\gamma_j=\beta\zeta_j\). The \(\zeta_j\) are distinct \(h\)-th
+  roots of unity, so \(s\le h\). If \(C_r=0\) for every
+  \(0\le r<h\), then
+  \begin{equation}
+    0=\beta^{-r}C_r
+      =\sum_{j=1}^s A_{\gamma_j}\zeta_j^r
+      \qquad(0\le r<h).
+      \label{eq:weak-perron-fourier-system}
+  \end{equation}
+  The \(h\times s\) Fourier--Vandermonde matrix
+  \[
+    (\zeta_j^r)_{\substack{0\le r<h\\1\le j\le s}}
+  \]
+  has full column rank: its first \(s\) rows form a square Vandermonde
+  matrix with determinant
+  \(\prod_{1\le i<j\le s}(\zeta_j-\zeta_i)\ne0\).
+  Equation \eqref{eq:weak-perron-fourier-system} would force all
+  peripheral coefficients to vanish,
+  including \(A_\beta\), a contradiction.
+
+  \emph{Cyclic propagation of positivity.}
+  Choose \(r\) with \(C_r>0\). If \(r<h-1\), then for all sufficiently
+  large \(n\), strict increase gives
+  \[
+    U_{hn+r}<U_{hn+r+1}.
+  \]
+  Divide by \(\rho^n\) and use
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-residue-asymptotic} for both residue classes. The
+  limiting inequality gives \(C_r\le C_{r+1}\), so in particular
+  \(C_{r+1}>0\). At the wraparound, strict increase gives
+  \begin{equation}
+    U_{hn+h-1}<U_{h(n+1)},
+    \qquad
+    \rho^{-n}U_{h(n+1)}\longrightarrow\rho C_0,
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-wraparound-limit}
+  \end{equation}
+  whereas \(\rho^{-n}U_{hn+h-1}\to C_{h-1}\). Thus
+  \(C_{h-1}\le\rho C_0\), and \(C_{h-1}>0\) forces \(C_0>0\).
+  Starting from one positive coefficient and moving cyclically proves
+  \begin{equation}
+    C_r>0\qquad(0\le r<h).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-positive-residues}
+  \end{equation}
+
+  Finally, if \(N=hn+r\), then
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-residue-asymptotic} and
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-positive-residues} give
+  \begin{align*}
+    U_N&=C_r\rho^n(1+o(1)),\\
+    \frac{\log U_N}{N}
+      &=\frac{n\log\rho+\log C_r+o(1)}{hn+r}
+        \longrightarrow\frac{\log\rho}{h}=\log\beta.
+  \end{align*}
+  There are only finitely many residues, so this proves the global limit
+  \begin{equation}
+    \lim_{N\to\infty}U_N^{1/N}=\beta.
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-global-root-limit}
+  \end{equation}

+For a standard greedy linear numeration basis with \(U_0=1\), a positive
