+  \(\gamma\) is any conjugate of \(\beta\), then
+  \[
+    \lvert\gamma\rvert=\beta\ \Longrightarrow\ \gamma^h=\rho,
+    \qquad
+    \lvert\gamma\rvert<\beta\ \Longrightarrow\
+      \lvert\gamma^h\rvert<\rho.
+  \]
+  In particular, every peripheral phase \(\gamma/\beta\) is an
+  \(h\)-th root of unity; the conclusion is stronger than merely placing
+  \(\gamma^h\) somewhere on the circle of radius \(\rho\).
+
+  \emph{Tail coefficients and their covariance.}
+  Put \(d=\deg\mu_U\), let \(K\) be a splitting field of \(\mu_U\), and
+  let \(J_{\mathrm r}\) be the threshold from which \(\mu_U\) annihilates
+  \(U\). The irreducible polynomial \(\mu_U\in\mathbb Q[X]\) is
+  separable. Hence there are unique coefficients \(A_\gamma\in K\), one
+  for each conjugate \(\gamma\) of \(\beta\), such that
+  \begin{equation}
+    U_n=\sum_\gamma A_\gamma\gamma^n
+    \qquad(n\ge J_{\mathrm r}).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-tail-expansion}
+  \end{equation}
+  Indeed, the coefficients are determined by the \(d\) values with
+  \(n=J_{\mathrm r},\ldots,J_{\mathrm r}+d-1\); the corresponding matrix
+  is a nonsingular Vandermonde matrix multiplied by the nonzero diagonal
+  matrix \(\operatorname{diag}(\gamma^{J_{\mathrm r}})\). No polynomial
+  factors in \(n\) occur because every root is simple.
+
+  For \(\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(K/\mathbb Q)\), applying \(\sigma\)
+  to \eqref{eq:weak-perron-tail-expansion} and using
+  \(U_n\in\mathbb Q\) gives
+  \[
+    U_n=\sum_\gamma \sigma(A_\gamma)\sigma(\gamma)^n.
+  \]
+  Uniqueness of the expansion therefore yields the explicit covariance
+  identity
+  \begin{equation}
+    A_{\sigma(\gamma)}=\sigma(A_\gamma).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-galois-covariance}
+  \end{equation}
+  For each conjugate \(\gamma\), the embedding
+  \(\mathbb Q(\beta)\hookrightarrow K\) that sends \(\beta\) to
+  \(\gamma\) extends to an automorphism of the splitting field \(K\).
+  Thus, if \(A_\beta=0\),
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-galois-covariance} forces every \(A_\gamma\) to vanish,
+  contradicting the positive, nonzero tail of \(U\). Consequently
+  \(A_\beta\ne0\); the same argument in fact shows that every
+  \(A_\gamma\ne0\).
+
+  \emph{Residue asymptotics.}
+  For each \(r\in\{0,\ldots,h-1\}\), set
+  \begin{equation}
+    N_r:=\max\!\left\{0,
+      \left\lceil\frac{J_{\mathrm r}-r}{h}\right\rceil\right\},
+    \qquad
+    C_r:=\sum_{\lvert\gamma\rvert=\beta}A_\gamma\gamma^r.
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-residue-threshold-coefficient}
+  \end{equation}
+  Then \(hn+r\ge J_{\mathrm r}\) whenever \(n\ge N_r\), so
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-tail-expansion} applies. For a peripheral conjugate,
+  \(\gamma^{hn+r}=\gamma^r\rho^n\).
+  If \(\lvert\gamma\rvert<\beta\), then
+  \(\lvert\gamma^h\rvert<\rho\). If such conjugates exist, their total
+  contribution is \(O(\theta^n)\), where
+  \(\theta=\max_{\lvert\gamma\rvert<\beta}\lvert\gamma\rvert^h<\rho\);
+  if none exist, that contribution is identically zero and we choose any
+  \(0<\theta<\rho\). Therefore, for
+  every fixed residue \(r\),
+  \begin{equation}
+    U_{hn+r}=C_r\rho^n+O(\theta^n)
+             =C_r\rho^n+o(\rho^n)
+    \qquad(n\ge N_r).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-residue-asymptotic}
+  \end{equation}
+  In particular,
+  \[
+    C_r=\lim_{n\to\infty}\rho^{-n}U_{hn+r}.
+  \]
+  The right-hand side is a limit of real nonnegative numbers, so
+  \(C_r\in\mathbb R\) and \(C_r\ge0\).
+
+  At least one residue coefficient is nonzero. To see this without any
+  suppressed independence argument, list the peripheral conjugates as
+  \(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_s\), and write
+  \(\gamma_j=\beta\zeta_j\). The \(\zeta_j\) are distinct \(h\)-th
+  roots of unity, so \(s\le h\). If \(C_r=0\) for every
+  \(0\le r<h\), then
+  \begin{equation}
+    0=\beta^{-r}C_r
+      =\sum_{j=1}^s A_{\gamma_j}\zeta_j^r
+      \qquad(0\le r<h).
+      \label{eq:weak-perron-fourier-system}
+  \end{equation}
+  The \(h\times s\) Fourier--Vandermonde matrix
+  \[
+    (\zeta_j^r)_{\substack{0\le r<h\\1\le j\le s}}
+  \]
+  has full column rank: its first \(s\) rows form a square Vandermonde
+  matrix with determinant
+  \(\prod_{1\le i<j\le s}(\zeta_j-\zeta_i)\ne0\).
+  Equation \eqref{eq:weak-perron-fourier-system} would force all
+  peripheral coefficients to vanish,
+  including \(A_\beta\), a contradiction.
+
+  \emph{Cyclic propagation of positivity.}
+  Choose \(r\) with \(C_r>0\). If \(r<h-1\), then for all sufficiently
+  large \(n\), strict increase gives
+  \[
+    U_{hn+r}<U_{hn+r+1}.
+  \]
+  Divide by \(\rho^n\) and use
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-residue-asymptotic} for both residue classes. The
+  limiting inequality gives \(C_r\le C_{r+1}\), so in particular
+  \(C_{r+1}>0\). At the wraparound, strict increase gives
+  \begin{equation}
+    U_{hn+h-1}<U_{h(n+1)},
+    \qquad
+    \rho^{-n}U_{h(n+1)}\longrightarrow\rho C_0,
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-wraparound-limit}
+  \end{equation}
+  whereas \(\rho^{-n}U_{hn+h-1}\to C_{h-1}\). Thus
+  \(C_{h-1}\le\rho C_0\), and \(C_{h-1}>0\) forces \(C_0>0\).
+  Starting from one positive coefficient and moving cyclically proves
+  \begin{equation}
+    C_r>0\qquad(0\le r<h).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-positive-residues}
+  \end{equation}
+
+  Finally, if \(N=hn+r\), then
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-residue-asymptotic} and
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-positive-residues} give
+  \begin{align*}
+    U_N&=C_r\rho^n(1+o(1)),\\
+    \frac{\log U_N}{N}
+      &=\frac{n\log\rho+\log C_r+o(1)}{hn+r}
+        \longrightarrow\frac{\log\rho}{h}=\log\beta.
+  \end{align*}
+  There are only finitely many residues, so this proves the global limit
+  \begin{equation}
+    \lim_{N\to\infty}U_N^{1/N}=\beta.
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-global-root-limit}
+  \end{equation}

+\paragraph{Greedy length interval.}
+For a standard greedy linear numeration basis with \(U_0=1\), a positive
+integer has a canonical greedy word of length \(m\) if and only if it lies
+in the half-open interval
+\[
+  [U_{m-1},U_m).
+\]
+Indeed, the greedy algorithm chooses the least threshold \(U_m\) strictly
+larger than the represented integer; minimality of \(m\) gives the lower
+bound, and the choice of \(U_m\) gives the upper bound. This is a property
+of the standard greedy subclass, not an assumption on the ambient
+canonical eventually recurrent systems.
+

+  We first establish the asymptotic needed for
+  \textup{(ii)}\(\Rightarrow\)\textup{(iii)}. This conclusion is also
+  obtainable from Charlier--Kreczman's quotient-limit mechanism
+  \cite[Proposition~10 and Remark~12]{CharlierKreczman2025}; we give the
+  coefficient-level argument because the residue thresholds and positivity
+  are part of the hypotheses used here.
+
+  \emph{Peripheral period.}
+  The classical power characterization of weak Perron numbers gives an
+  integer \(h\ge1\) for which
+  \[
+    \rho:=\beta^h
+  \]
+  is a Perron number \cite{Brunotte2013,Lind1984}. Equivalently, if
+  \(\gamma\) is any conjugate of \(\beta\), then
+  \[
+    \lvert\gamma\rvert=\beta\ \Longrightarrow\ \gamma^h=\rho,
+    \qquad
+    \lvert\gamma\rvert<\beta\ \Longrightarrow\
+      \lvert\gamma^h\rvert<\rho.
+  \]
+  In particular, every peripheral phase \(\gamma/\beta\) is an
+  \(h\)-th root of unity; the conclusion is stronger than merely placing
+  \(\gamma^h\) somewhere on the circle of radius \(\rho\).
+
+  \emph{Tail coefficients and their covariance.}
+  Put \(d=\deg\mu_U\), let \(K\) be a splitting field of \(\mu_U\), and
+  let \(J_{\mathrm r}\) be the threshold from which \(\mu_U\) annihilates
+  \(U\). The irreducible polynomial \(\mu_U\in\mathbb Q[X]\) is
+  separable. Hence there are unique coefficients \(A_\gamma\in K\), one
+  for each conjugate \(\gamma\) of \(\beta\), such that
+  \begin{equation}
+    U_n=\sum_\gamma A_\gamma\gamma^n
+    \qquad(n\ge J_{\mathrm r}).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-tail-expansion}
+  \end{equation}
+  Indeed, the coefficients are determined by the \(d\) values with
+  \(n=J_{\mathrm r},\ldots,J_{\mathrm r}+d-1\); the corresponding matrix
+  is a nonsingular Vandermonde matrix multiplied by the nonzero diagonal
+  matrix \(\operatorname{diag}(\gamma^{J_{\mathrm r}})\). No polynomial
+  factors in \(n\) occur because every root is simple.
+
+  For \(\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(K/\mathbb Q)\), applying \(\sigma\)
+  to \eqref{eq:weak-perron-tail-expansion} and using
+  \(U_n\in\mathbb Q\) gives
+  \[
+    U_n=\sum_\gamma \sigma(A_\gamma)\sigma(\gamma)^n.
+  \]
+  Uniqueness of the expansion therefore yields the explicit covariance
+  identity
+  \begin{equation}
+    A_{\sigma(\gamma)}=\sigma(A_\gamma).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-galois-covariance}
+  \end{equation}
+  For each conjugate \(\gamma\), the embedding
+  \(\mathbb Q(\beta)\hookrightarrow K\) that sends \(\beta\) to
+  \(\gamma\) extends to an automorphism of the splitting field \(K\).
+  Thus, if \(A_\beta=0\),
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-galois-covariance} forces every \(A_\gamma\) to vanish,
+  contradicting the positive, nonzero tail of \(U\). Consequently
+  \(A_\beta\ne0\); the same argument in fact shows that every
+  \(A_\gamma\ne0\).
+
+  \emph{Residue asymptotics.}
+  For each \(r\in\{0,\ldots,h-1\}\), set
+  \begin{equation}
+    N_r:=\max\!\left\{0,
+      \left\lceil\frac{J_{\mathrm r}-r}{h}\right\rceil\right\},
+    \qquad
+    C_r:=\sum_{\lvert\gamma\rvert=\beta}A_\gamma\gamma^r.
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-residue-threshold-coefficient}
+  \end{equation}
+  Then \(hn+r\ge J_{\mathrm r}\) whenever \(n\ge N_r\), so
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-tail-expansion} applies. For a peripheral conjugate,
+  \(\gamma^{hn+r}=\gamma^r\rho^n\).
+  If \(\lvert\gamma\rvert<\beta\), then
+  \(\lvert\gamma^h\rvert<\rho\). If such conjugates exist, their total
+  contribution is \(O(\theta^n)\), where
+  \(\theta=\max_{\lvert\gamma\rvert<\beta}\lvert\gamma\rvert^h<\rho\);
+  if none exist, that contribution is identically zero and we choose any
+  \(0<\theta<\rho\). Therefore, for
+  every fixed residue \(r\),
+  \begin{equation}
+    U_{hn+r}=C_r\rho^n+O(\theta^n)
+             =C_r\rho^n+o(\rho^n)
+    \qquad(n\ge N_r).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-residue-asymptotic}
+  \end{equation}
+  In particular,
+  \[
+    C_r=\lim_{n\to\infty}\rho^{-n}U_{hn+r}.
+  \]
+  The right-hand side is a limit of real nonnegative numbers, so
+  \(C_r\in\mathbb R\) and \(C_r\ge0\).
+
+  At least one residue coefficient is nonzero. To see this without any
+  suppressed independence argument, list the peripheral conjugates as
+  \(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_s\), and write
+  \(\gamma_j=\beta\zeta_j\). The \(\zeta_j\) are distinct \(h\)-th
+  roots of unity, so \(s\le h\). If \(C_r=0\) for every
+  \(0\le r<h\), then
+  \begin{equation}
+    0=\beta^{-r}C_r
+      =\sum_{j=1}^s A_{\gamma_j}\zeta_j^r
+      \qquad(0\le r<h).
+      \label{eq:weak-perron-fourier-system}
+  \end{equation}
+  The \(h\times s\) Fourier--Vandermonde matrix
+  \[
+    (\zeta_j^r)_{\substack{0\le r<h\\1\le j\le s}}
+  \]
+  has full column rank: its first \(s\) rows form a square Vandermonde
+  matrix with determinant
+  \(\prod_{1\le i<j\le s}(\zeta_j-\zeta_i)\ne0\).
+  Equation \eqref{eq:weak-perron-fourier-system} would force all
+  peripheral coefficients to vanish,
+  including \(A_\beta\), a contradiction.
+
+  \emph{Cyclic propagation of positivity.}
+  Choose \(r\) with \(C_r>0\). If \(r<h-1\), then for all sufficiently
+  large \(n\), strict increase gives
+  \[
+    U_{hn+r}<U_{hn+r+1}.
+  \]
+  Divide by \(\rho^n\) and use
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-residue-asymptotic} for both residue classes. The
+  limiting inequality gives \(C_r\le C_{r+1}\), so in particular
+  \(C_{r+1}>0\). At the wraparound, strict increase gives
+  \begin{equation}
+    U_{hn+h-1}<U_{h(n+1)},
+    \qquad
+    \rho^{-n}U_{h(n+1)}\longrightarrow\rho C_0,
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-wraparound-limit}
+  \end{equation}
+  whereas \(\rho^{-n}U_{hn+h-1}\to C_{h-1}\). Thus
+  \(C_{h-1}\le\rho C_0\), and \(C_{h-1}>0\) forces \(C_0>0\).
+  Starting from one positive coefficient and moving cyclically proves
+  \begin{equation}
+    C_r>0\qquad(0\le r<h).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-positive-residues}
+  \end{equation}
+
+  Finally, if \(N=hn+r\), then
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-residue-asymptotic} and
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-positive-residues} give
+  \begin{align*}
+    U_N&=C_r\rho^n(1+o(1)),\\
+    \frac{\log U_N}{N}
+      &=\frac{n\log\rho+\log C_r+o(1)}{hn+r}
+        \longrightarrow\frac{\log\rho}{h}=\log\beta.
+  \end{align*}
+  There are only finitely many residues, so this proves the global limit
+  \begin{equation}
+    \lim_{N\to\infty}U_N^{1/N}=\beta.
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-global-root-limit}
+  \end{equation}

**Peripheral-Spectrum Proof**

Theorem 2.25 remains mathematically unchanged, but its highest-risk implication is now written out at referee standard. The detailed argument is isolated in [sec_pisot_weak_perron_analysis.tex](D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_prime_languages_finite_state_obstructions_monatshefte/sec_pisot_weak_perron_analysis.tex:1), included from the theorem proof in [sec_pisot_part2.tex](D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_prime_languages_finite_state_obstructions_monatshefte/sec_pisot_part2.tex:668).

The expansion supplies all details previously omitted:

- The classical weak-Perron power characterization is stated explicitly: there is an \(h\geq1\) such that \(\rho=\beta^h\) is Perron, every peripheral conjugate satisfies \(\gamma^h=\rho\), and every smaller conjugate remains strictly smaller after the \(h\)-th power.
- The tail threshold \(J_{\mathrm r}\), splitting field \(K\), degree \(d\), and unique coefficients \(A_\gamma\) are introduced explicitly.
- Uniqueness of the tail expansion is proved from \(d\) consecutive values and the nonsingular Vandermonde matrix.
- Galois covariance is displayed as
  \[
  A_{\sigma(\gamma)}=\sigma(A_\gamma),
  \]
  including the extension of embeddings \(\mathbb Q(\beta)\hookrightarrow K\) to splitting-field automorphisms.
- The proof that \(A_\beta\neq0\), and in fact every \(A_\gamma\neq0\), is now complete.
- Every residue has an explicit threshold
  \[
  N_r=\max\left\{0,\left\lceil\frac{J_{\mathrm r}-r}{h}\right\rceil\right\}
  \]
  and coefficient
  \[
  C_r=\sum_{|\gamma|=\beta}A_\gamma\gamma^r.
  \]
- The nonperipheral tail is handled explicitly, including the case where no smaller conjugates exist.
- Reality and nonnegativity of \(C_r\) follow from the displayed limit \(\rho^{-n}U_{hn+r}\to C_r\).
- The Fourier–Vandermonde argument now identifies the distinct \(h\)-th-root phases, notes \(s\leq h\), displays the \(h\times s\) matrix, and proves full column rank using its first \(s\) rows.
- Cyclic positivity includes the wraparound factor
  \[
  \rho^{-n}U_{h(n+1)}\longrightarrow \rho C_0.
  \]
- The residue asymptotics are converted explicitly into the global limit \(U_N^{1/N}\to\beta\).
- The greedy interval property is separately stated and justified in [sec_pisot_part2.tex](D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_prime_languages_finite_state_obstructions_monatshefte/sec_pisot_part2.tex:483).
- The final length squeeze now shows both threshold sequences converge to \(\beta^D\) after taking \(t\)-th roots.
- The minimal tail recurrence is formally defined as the monic generator of the tail-annihilator ideal in [sec_pisot_part1.tex](D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_prime_languages_finite_state_obstructions_monatshefte/sec_pisot_part1.tex:630), making the binomial divisibility and eventual scalar-periodicity equivalence immediate.

I also incorporated the referee’s two smaller points: the finite-word restriction is now written as \(L^{\ge J}=L\cap A^{\ge J}\), and the length-order audit says “the general theorem chain for recurrent numeration,” avoiding a literally overbroad claim.

**Charlier–Kreczman Comparison**

I read the complete 51-page arXiv v1 before writing the comparison.

My assessment agrees with the referee and is now stated plainly in the manuscript:

- Charlier–Kreczman give a full characterization of regularity of the whole greedy language for positional numeration systems without assuming a dominant root. Their criteria use the associated periodic alternate base and the graph of greedy and quasi-greedy expansions of \(1\). Their general procedure is a semidecision and becomes a decision procedure when the associated alternate base is known to be Parry.
- Their Proposition 10 derives residue-class consecutive-quotient limits from regularity of the whole language.
- More importantly for this manuscript, their Remark 12 states the converse quotient-limit mechanism for an arbitrary linear recurrence when the dominating eigenvalues have a common \(p\)-th power and the term moduli are eventually increasing.
- Under Theorem 2.25’s hypotheses, separability gives equal peripheral multiplicities, weak-Perron periodicity gives the common power, and strict increase supplies the eventual-increase hypothesis. Therefore, the asymptotic mechanism used by the greedy-length squeeze is already present there in essentially equivalent quotient-limit form. It is no longer presented as new.
- Their paper does not treat MCFL sublanguages, bounded prime support, synchronized geometric schemes, Evertse’s quotient rigidity, or the five-way radical/scalar-periodicity classification.
- Conversely, this paper does not characterize regularity of the whole greedy language. Its remaining contribution is the passage from bounded outside-prime support on an infinite finite-fan-out MCFL to an exact synchronized geometric ray, followed by the weak-Perron algebraic classification of that phenomenon.

The citation and comparison now appear:

- In the main-results introduction and dedicated prior-work discussion: [sec_introduction.tex](D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_prime_languages_finite_state_obstructions_monatshefte/sec_introduction.tex:132)
- In the statement of Theorem 2.25 itself: [sec_pisot_part2.tex](D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_prime_languages_finite_state_obstructions_monatshefte/sec_pisot_part2.tex:617)
- Again at the start of the coefficient-level proof: [sec_pisot_weak_perron_analysis.tex](D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_prime_languages_finite_state_obstructions_monatshefte/sec_pisot_weak_perron_analysis.tex:1)
- In the bibliography, together with Brunotte’s direct weak-Perron reference: [references.tex](D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_prime_languages_finite_state_obstructions_monatshefte/references.tex:91)
- In the reproducibility literature audit: [literature_check.md](D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_prime_languages_finite_state_obstructions_monatshefte/artifacts/literature_check.md:425)

The Seki–Matsumura–Fujii–Kasami priority wording remains intact. The one-synchronized-orbit ceiling remains explicit in the abstract, introduction, and conclusion. The text still denies control of every sufficiently long word, the whole canonical language, and simultaneous representations in two systems. The general geometric-scheme decision problem and Caucal–Le Gonidec degeneracy/Cobham-extension problem remain open. The \(\sqrt{pq}\) alternating-radix family and the nonintegral, nonunit Pisot example are unchanged.

+\paragraph{Greedy length interval.}
+For a standard greedy linear numeration basis with \(U_0=1\), a positive
+integer has a canonical greedy word of length \(m\) if and only if it lies
+in the half-open interval
+\[
+  [U_{m-1},U_m).
+\]
+Indeed, the greedy algorithm chooses the least threshold \(U_m\) strictly
+larger than the represented integer; minimality of \(m\) gives the lower
+bound, and the choice of \(U_m\) gives the upper bound. This is a property
+of the standard greedy subclass, not an assumption on the ambient
+canonical eventually recurrent systems.

+  We first establish the asymptotic needed for
+  \textup{(ii)}\(\Rightarrow\)\textup{(iii)}. This conclusion is also
+  obtainable from Charlier--Kreczman's quotient-limit mechanism
+  \cite[Proposition~10 and Remark~12]{CharlierKreczman2025}; we give the
+  coefficient-level argument because the residue thresholds and positivity
+  are part of the hypotheses used here.
+
+  \emph{Peripheral period.}
+  The classical power characterization of weak Perron numbers gives an
+  integer \(h\ge1\) for which
+  \[
+    \rho:=\beta^h
+  \]
+  is a Perron number \cite{Brunotte2013,Lind1984}. Equivalently, if
+  \(\gamma\) is any conjugate of \(\beta\), then
+  \[
+    \lvert\gamma\rvert=\beta\ \Longrightarrow\ \gamma^h=\rho,
+    \qquad
+    \lvert\gamma\rvert<\beta\ \Longrightarrow\
+      \lvert\gamma^h\rvert<\rho.
+  \]
+  In particular, every peripheral phase \(\gamma/\beta\) is an
+  \(h\)-th root of unity; the conclusion is stronger than merely placing
+  \(\gamma^h\) somewhere on the circle of radius \(\rho\).
+
+  \emph{Tail coefficients and their covariance.}
+  Put \(d=\deg\mu_U\), let \(K\) be a splitting field of \(\mu_U\), and
+  let \(J_{\mathrm r}\) be the threshold from which \(\mu_U\) annihilates
+  \(U\). The irreducible polynomial \(\mu_U\in\mathbb Q[X]\) is
+  separable. Hence there are unique coefficients \(A_\gamma\in K\), one
+  for each conjugate \(\gamma\) of \(\beta\), such that
+  \begin{equation}
+    U_n=\sum_\gamma A_\gamma\gamma^n
+    \qquad(n\ge J_{\mathrm r}).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-tail-expansion}
+  \end{equation}
+  Indeed, the coefficients are determined by the \(d\) values with
+  \(n=J_{\mathrm r},\ldots,J_{\mathrm r}+d-1\); the corresponding matrix
+  is a nonsingular Vandermonde matrix multiplied by the nonzero diagonal
+  matrix \(\operatorname{diag}(\gamma^{J_{\mathrm r}})\). No polynomial
+  factors in \(n\) occur because every root is simple.
+
+  For \(\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(K/\mathbb Q)\), applying \(\sigma\)
+  to \eqref{eq:weak-perron-tail-expansion} and using
+  \(U_n\in\mathbb Q\) gives
+  \[
+    U_n=\sum_\gamma \sigma(A_\gamma)\sigma(\gamma)^n.
+  \]
+  Uniqueness of the expansion therefore yields the explicit covariance
+  identity
+  \begin{equation}
+    A_{\sigma(\gamma)}=\sigma(A_\gamma).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-galois-covariance}
+  \end{equation}
+  For each conjugate \(\gamma\), the embedding
+  \(\mathbb Q(\beta)\hookrightarrow K\) that sends \(\beta\) to
+  \(\gamma\) extends to an automorphism of the splitting field \(K\).
+  Thus, if \(A_\beta=0\),
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-galois-covariance} forces every \(A_\gamma\) to vanish,
+  contradicting the positive, nonzero tail of \(U\). Consequently
+  \(A_\beta\ne0\); the same argument in fact shows that every
+  \(A_\gamma\ne0\).
+
+  \emph{Residue asymptotics.}
+  For each \(r\in\{0,\ldots,h-1\}\), set
+  \begin{equation}
+    N_r:=\max\!\left\{0,
+      \left\lceil\frac{J_{\mathrm r}-r}{h}\right\rceil\right\},
+    \qquad
+    C_r:=\sum_{\lvert\gamma\rvert=\beta}A_\gamma\gamma^r.
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-residue-threshold-coefficient}
+  \end{equation}
+  Then \(hn+r\ge J_{\mathrm r}\) whenever \(n\ge N_r\), so
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-tail-expansion} applies. For a peripheral conjugate,
+  \(\gamma^{hn+r}=\gamma^r\rho^n\).
+  If \(\lvert\gamma\rvert<\beta\), then
+  \(\lvert\gamma^h\rvert<\rho\). If such conjugates exist, their total
+  contribution is \(O(\theta^n)\), where
+  \(\theta=\max_{\lvert\gamma\rvert<\beta}\lvert\gamma\rvert^h<\rho\);
+  if none exist, that contribution is identically zero and we choose any
+  \(0<\theta<\rho\). Therefore, for
+  every fixed residue \(r\),
+  \begin{equation}
+    U_{hn+r}=C_r\rho^n+O(\theta^n)
+             =C_r\rho^n+o(\rho^n)
+    \qquad(n\ge N_r).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-residue-asymptotic}
+  \end{equation}
+  In particular,
+  \[
+    C_r=\lim_{n\to\infty}\rho^{-n}U_{hn+r}.
+  \]
+  The right-hand side is a limit of real nonnegative numbers, so
+  \(C_r\in\mathbb R\) and \(C_r\ge0\).
+
+  At least one residue coefficient is nonzero. To see this without any
+  suppressed independence argument, list the peripheral conjugates as
+  \(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_s\), and write
+  \(\gamma_j=\beta\zeta_j\). The \(\zeta_j\) are distinct \(h\)-th
+  roots of unity, so \(s\le h\). If \(C_r=0\) for every
+  \(0\le r<h\), then
+  \begin{equation}
+    0=\beta^{-r}C_r
+      =\sum_{j=1}^s A_{\gamma_j}\zeta_j^r
+      \qquad(0\le r<h).
+      \label{eq:weak-perron-fourier-system}
+  \end{equation}
+  The \(h\times s\) Fourier--Vandermonde matrix
+  \[
+    (\zeta_j^r)_{\substack{0\le r<h\\1\le j\le s}}
+  \]
+  has full column rank: its first \(s\) rows form a square Vandermonde
+  matrix with determinant
+  \(\prod_{1\le i<j\le s}(\zeta_j-\zeta_i)\ne0\).
+  Equation \eqref{eq:weak-perron-fourier-system} would force all
+  peripheral coefficients to vanish,
+  including \(A_\beta\), a contradiction.
+
+  \emph{Cyclic propagation of positivity.}
+  Choose \(r\) with \(C_r>0\). If \(r<h-1\), then for all sufficiently
+  large \(n\), strict increase gives
+  \[
+    U_{hn+r}<U_{hn+r+1}.
+  \]
+  Divide by \(\rho^n\) and use
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-residue-asymptotic} for both residue classes. The
+  limiting inequality gives \(C_r\le C_{r+1}\), so in particular
+  \(C_{r+1}>0\). At the wraparound, strict increase gives
+  \begin{equation}
+    U_{hn+h-1}<U_{h(n+1)},
+    \qquad
+    \rho^{-n}U_{h(n+1)}\longrightarrow\rho C_0,
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-wraparound-limit}
+  \end{equation}
+  whereas \(\rho^{-n}U_{hn+h-1}\to C_{h-1}\). Thus
+  \(C_{h-1}\le\rho C_0\), and \(C_{h-1}>0\) forces \(C_0>0\).
+  Starting from one positive coefficient and moving cyclically proves
+  \begin{equation}
+    C_r>0\qquad(0\le r<h).
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-positive-residues}
+  \end{equation}
+
+  Finally, if \(N=hn+r\), then
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-residue-asymptotic} and
+  \eqref{eq:weak-perron-positive-residues} give
+  \begin{align*}
+    U_N&=C_r\rho^n(1+o(1)),\\
+    \frac{\log U_N}{N}
+      &=\frac{n\log\rho+\log C_r+o(1)}{hn+r}
+        \longrightarrow\frac{\log\rho}{h}=\log\beta.
+  \end{align*}
+  There are only finitely many residues, so this proves the global limit
+  \begin{equation}
+    \lim_{N\to\infty}U_N^{1/N}=\beta.
+    \label{eq:weak-perron-global-root-limit}
+  \end{equation}

**Peripheral-Spectrum Proof**

The detailed argument is isolated in [sec_pisot_weak_perron_analysis.tex](D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_prime_languages_finite_state_obstructions_monatshefte/sec_pisot_weak_perron_analysis.tex:1), included from the theorem proof in [sec_pisot_part2.tex](D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_prime_languages_finite_state_obstructions_monatshefte/sec_pisot_part2.tex:668).

The expansion supplies all details previously omitted:

- The classical weak-Perron power characterization is stated explicitly: there is an \(h\geq1\) such that \(\rho=\beta^h\) is Perron, every peripheral conjugate satisfies \(\gamma^h=\rho\), and every smaller conjugate remains strictly smaller after the \(h\)-th power.
- The tail threshold \(J_{\mathrm r}\), splitting field \(K\), degree \(d\), and unique coefficients \(A_\gamma\) are introduced explicitly.
- Uniqueness of the tail expansion is proved from \(d\) consecutive values and the nonsingular Vandermonde matrix.
- Galois covariance is displayed as
  \[
  A_{\sigma(\gamma)}=\sigma(A_\gamma),
  \]
  including the extension of embeddings \(\mathbb Q(\beta)\hookrightarrow K\) to splitting-field automorphisms.
- The proof that \(A_\beta\neq0\), and in fact every \(A_\gamma\neq0\), is now complete.
- Every residue has an explicit threshold
  \[
  N_r=\max\left\{0,\left\lceil\frac{J_{\mathrm r}-r}{h}\right\rceil\right\}
  \]
  and coefficient
  \[
  C_r=\sum_{|\gamma|=\beta}A_\gamma\gamma^r.
  \]
- The nonperipheral tail is handled explicitly, including the case where no smaller conjugates exist.
- Reality and nonnegativity of \(C_r\) follow from the displayed limit \(\rho^{-n}U_{hn+r}\to C_r\).
- The Fourier–Vandermonde argument now identifies the distinct \(h\)-th-root phases, notes \(s\leq h\), displays the \(h\times s\) matrix, and proves full column rank using its first \(s\) rows.
- Cyclic positivity includes the wraparound factor
  \[
  \rho^{-n}U_{h(n+1)}\longrightarrow \rho C_0.
  \]
- The residue asymptotics are converted explicitly into the global limit \(U_N^{1/N}\to\beta\).
- The greedy interval property is separately stated and justified in [sec_pisot_part2.tex](D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_prime_languages_finite_state_obstructions_monatshefte/sec_pisot_part2.tex:483).
- The final length squeeze now shows both threshold sequences converge to \(\beta^D\) after taking \(t\)-th roots.
- The minimal tail recurrence is formally defined as the monic generator of the tail-annihilator ideal in [sec_pisot_part1.tex](D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_prime_languages_finite_state_obstructions_monatshefte/sec_pisot_part1.tex:630), making the binomial divisibility and eventual scalar-periodicity equivalence immediate.

I also incorporated the referee’s two smaller points: the finite-word restriction is now written as \(L^{\ge J}=L\cap A^{\ge J}\), and the length-order audit says “the general theorem chain for recurrent numeration,” avoiding a literally overbroad claim.

**Charlier–Kreczman Comparison**

I read the complete 51-page arXiv v1 before writing the comparison.

My assessment agrees with the referee and is now stated plainly in the manuscript:

- Charlier–Kreczman give a full characterization of regularity of the whole greedy language for positional numeration systems without assuming a dominant root. Their criteria use the associated periodic alternate base and the graph of greedy and quasi-greedy expansions of \(1\). Their general procedure is a semidecision and becomes a decision procedure when the associated alternate base is known to be Parry.
- Their Proposition 10 derives residue-class consecutive-quotient limits from regularity of the whole language.
- More importantly for this manuscript, their Remark 12 states the converse quotient-limit mechanism for an arbitrary linear recurrence when the dominating eigenvalues have a common \(p\)-th power and the term moduli are eventually increasing.
- Under Theorem 2.25’s hypotheses, separability gives equal peripheral multiplicities, weak-Perron periodicity gives the common power, and strict increase supplies the eventual-increase hypothesis. Therefore, the asymptotic mechanism used by the greedy-length squeeze is already present there in essentially equivalent quotient-limit form. It is no longer presented as new.
- Their paper does not treat MCFL sublanguages, bounded prime support, synchronized geometric schemes, Evertse’s quotient rigidity, or the five-way radical/scalar-periodicity classification.
- Conversely, this paper does not characterize regularity of the whole greedy language. Its remaining contribution is the passage from bounded outside-prime support on an infinite finite-fan-out MCFL to an exact synchronized geometric ray, followed by the weak-Perron algebraic classification of that phenomenon.

The citation and comparison now appear:

- In the main-results introduction and dedicated prior-work discussion: [sec_introduction.tex](D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_prime_languages_finite_state_obstructions_monatshefte/sec_introduction.tex:132)
- In the statement of Theorem 2.25 itself: [sec_pisot_part2.tex](D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_prime_languages_finite_state_obstructions_monatshefte/sec_pisot_part2.tex:617)
- Again at the start of the coefficient-level proof: [sec_pisot_weak_perron_analysis.tex](D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_prime_languages_finite_state_obstructions_monatshefte/sec_pisot_weak_perron_analysis.tex:1)
- In the bibliography, together with Brunotte’s direct weak-Perron reference: [references.tex](D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_prime_languages_finite_state_obstructions_monatshefte/references.tex:91)
- In the reproducibility literature audit: [literature_check.md](D:/omega/automath/papers/publication/2026_prime_languages_finite_state_obstructions_monatshefte/artifacts/literature_check.md:425)

The Seki–Matsumura–Fujii–Kasami priority wording remains intact. The one-synchronized-orbit ceiling remains explicit in the abstract, introduction, and conclusion. The text still denies control of every sufficiently long word, the whole canonical language, and simultaneous representations in two systems. The general geometric-scheme decision problem and Caucal–Le Gonidec degeneracy/Cobham-extension problem remain open. The \(\sqrt{pq}\) alternating-radix family and the nonintegral, nonunit Pisot example are unchanged.
